area: ghcr.io/ublue-os/aurora (Universal Blue Aurora, KDE/Fedora bootc) — base-image selection, tag scheme, update mechanism, signing, and derived-image build, as of 2026-09-20

facts.claim: The current stable tag is `stable-20260915.2` and `ghcr.io/ublue-os/aurora:stable` resolves to digest sha256:911281f2aaa42bfd17532c5cef917aba8d7ac8c0faeb1c1edc6a43dc28d0d2f1 (verified live against the GHCR registry API today). Image config labels: org.opencontainers.image.version=44.20260915.2, ostree.linux=7.1.8-200.fc44.x86_64, created 2026-09-15T20:28:34Z, revision c6a79ae03b7a4e7c8119615fe7099f1f00cb949e.
facts.evidence: curl ghcr.io/v2/ublue-os/aurora/manifests/stable -> Docker-Content-Digest: sha256:911281f2aaa42bfd17532c5cef917aba8d7ac8c0faeb1c1edc6a43dc28d0d2f1 ; config blob sha256:bee8b5d7b53b618922b05259cd78f3cc4ddd792e4e5b09bcc9c8565c84e9b4dc labels. Also `gh api repos/ublue-os/aurora/releases` newest tag = stable-20260915.2
facts.impact: This is the literal digest to pin FROM. Note stable-20260915.2 and :stable are the same manifest, so pinning `ghcr.io/ublue-os/aurora:stable@sha256:9112...` gives you both a human-readable stream name and immutability.

facts.claim: `stable-daily` is NOT a separate, faster stream — it is an explicit legacy alias pushed alongside every `stable` build and currently resolves to the identical digest sha256:911281f2... Do not treat it as a daily channel.
facts.evidence:
ublue-os/aurora Justfile, generate-build-tags recipe, lines ~634-641: `if [[ "{{ tag }}" == stable ]]; then
  # Legacy Compatibility Tag so stable-daily points to stable, do not remove this
  # TODO: Move this to :latest after the ZFS removal to get daily updates again
  BUILD_TAGS+=("{{ tag }}-daily")`. Confirmed live: both `stable` and `stable-daily` return Docker-Content-Digest sha256:911281f2aaa42bfd17532c5cef917aba8d7ac8c0faeb1c1edc6a43dc28d0d2f1.
facts.impact: Removes a common mis-pin. `stable` and `stable-daily` are interchangeable today; pick `stable`.

facts.claim: There is no `lts` and no `gts` tag on ghcr.io/ublue-os/aurora. Manifest requests for `lts`, `gts` and `beta` return no digest (404). Only three real streams exist: stable, latest, testing.
facts.evidence: Registry manifest HEAD for tags lts/gts/beta returned <MISSING>; docs.getaurora.dev/guides/release-streams/ documents exactly three streams (Stable, Latest, Testing).
facts.impact: If the plan assumed an `lts` tag for the fleet, that is wrong — `lts` is a Bluefin (CentOS-bootc-based) concept, not an Aurora one. Use `:stable`.

facts.claim: `:stable` is the correct choice for a fleet that must not break. Stable builds weekly (Tuesday 01:00 UTC cron) off the `stable-f44` branch and rides a gated kernel that tracks Fedora CoreOS stable rather than Fedora Kinoite. Latest rebuilds on every push to `stable-f44` (currently latest-44.20260920.2 with kernel 7.2.5-200.fc44). Testing tracks `main` and is already on Fedora 45 (testing-45.20260920.5, kernel 7.2.5-300.fc45).
facts.evidence: .github/workflows/trigger-schedule-stable-image.yml: `schedule: - cron: "0 1 * * TUE"`; build-image-stable.yml has no push trigger (comment: "we are only publishing weekly :stable images"). docs.getaurora.dev/guides/release-streams/: "The stable stream is the recommended choice for most users". Live labels for :latest and :testing as above.
facts.impact: Pin `:stable` by digest and bump deliberately once a week after a canary. Expect a Fedora 45 rebase to land on stable in a few weeks — plan a validation gate for the F44→F45 jump, since main has already moved (image-versions.yml pins quay.io/fedora-ostree-desktops/kinoite tag 45).

facts.claim: `ghcr.io/ublue-os/aurora:stable` is x86_64 ONLY. The manifest is a single OCI image manifest, not a multi-arch index, and the build matrix has aarch64 commented out.
facts.evidence: Manifest for :stable is `{"schemaVersion":2,"config":{...},"layers":[...]}` with no `manifests` array. build-image-stable.yml: `# Enable ARM when it makes sense` / `architecture: '["x86_64"]'`.
facts.impact: Any arm64 machines in the fleet cannot use this base. Plan x86_64 only.

facts.claim: Contents of :stable — Fedora 44, KDE Plasma 6.7.5-1, kernel 7.1.8-200, Mesa 26.2.2-1, Podman 5.8.4-1, bootc 1.16.10-1, Flatpak 1.18.2-1, OSTree 2026.4-1, rpm-ostree 2026.2-1, NVIDIA 615.71.09-1 (nvidia-open variant).
facts.evidence: GitHub release body for tag stable-20260915.2, "Major packages" table.
facts.impact: Gives exact versions to test against; note bootc 1.16.x means `bootc switch`/`bootc upgrade` semantics, and rpm-ostree is still present for the non-composefs path.

facts.claim: Codecs and hardware acceleration are already fully handled: ffmpeg/ffmpeg-libs, libavcodec, libfdk-aac, libva-utils, pipewire-libs-extra and uld come from the negativo17 `fedora-multimedia` repo, and mesa/intel media stacks (intel-gmmlib, intel-mediasdk, intel-vpl-gpu-rt, libva, libva-intel-media-driver, mesa-*, libheif) are distro-synced from that repo and then version-locked. intel-vaapi-driver is added on x86_64.
facts.evidence: build_scripts/base/01-packages.sh: OVERRIDES array + `dnf5 distro-sync --skip-unavailable -y --repo='fedora-multimedia' "${OVERRIDES[@]}"` then `dnf5 versionlock add "${OVERRIDES[@]}"`; NEGATIVO_PACKAGES array.
facts.impact: Do not re-add RPM Fusion or reinstall ffmpeg in your derived layer — you will fight the versionlock and the negativo17 priority=90 setting.

facts.claim: distrobox, ujust, and Homebrew are all preinstalled. `distrobox` is an RPM in FEDORA_PACKAGES; `ujust` ships at /usr/bin/ujust with just recipes in /usr/share/ublue-os/just/*.just; Homebrew is layered in from ghcr.io/ublue-os/brew and brew-setup.service is preset-enabled.
facts.evidence: 01-packages.sh FEDORA_PACKAGES includes `distrobox` and `just`. Containerfile.in: `FROM ${BREW} AS brew` / `COPY --from=brew /system_files /system_files/shared`. system_files/shared/usr/lib/systemd/system-preset/89-aurora.preset: `enable brew-setup.service`. get-aurora-dev/common ships system_files/shared/usr/bin/ujust and usr/share/ublue-os/just/{00-entry,apps,changelog,default,shared,system,update}.just.
facts.impact: Nothing to add for these three. Your derived image can drop its own recipes into /usr/share/ublue-os/just/ and they are picked up by ujust.

facts.claim: Prunable bloat is mostly Flatpaks and a few desktop extras, not RPMs. The image preinstalls 22 system Flatpaks via a Brewfile (Firefox, Thunderbird, Kontact, DejaDup, Haruna, Gwenview, Okular, KWeather, KClock, KCalc, Qrca, Skanpage, Deskflow, MediaWriter, MissionCenter, Flatseal, Warehouse, Kontainer, KTailctl, Firmware, Breeze Gtk3 theme, Bazaar) plus a Bazaar flatpak preinstall drop-in. On the RPM side, aurora already removes firefox, plasma-discover, akonadi-server, khelpcenter, kcharselect, fedora-third-party, krfb and friends. Remaining RPM-side prune candidates for a managed fleet: sunshine (remote game streaming, from the lizardbyte COPR), kairpods, tailscale + tailscaled.service (preset-enabled), input-remapper, solaar/openrgb/libratbag udev rules, the fcitx5-* IME set, the full tesseract langpack set, and the google-noto CJK font set (~165 MB across four chunkah layers).
facts.evidence: get-aurora-dev/common system_files/shared/usr/share/ublue-os/homebrew/system-flatpaks.Brewfile (22 entries); aurora system_files/shared/usr/share/flatpak/preinstall.d/bazaar.preinstall; 01-packages.sh EXCLUDED_PACKAGES array and the sunshine/kairpods/tailscale install lines; 89-aurora.preset `enable tailscaled.service`; :stable manifest layer annotations org.chunkah.component rpm/google-noto-sans-cjk-fonts (102340014 bytes), rpm/google-noto-sans-cjk-vf-fonts (36732894), rpm/google-noto-serif-cjk-vf-fonts (25953949).
facts.impact: Cheapest wins: override system-flatpaks.Brewfile and delete /usr/share/flatpak/preinstall.d/bazaar.preinstall, and `systemctl disable tailscaled.service` (or mask it) in your layer. RPM removals are riskier because of the versionlocks.

facts.claim: Updates are driven by **uupd**, not bootc-fetch-apply-updates, not rpm-ostreed-automatic, not topgrade. The unit/timer names are exactly `uupd.service`, `uupd.timer` and `uupd-manual.service`. uupd.timer is enabled by systemd preset and fires OnCalendar=*-*-* 04:00:00 with Persistent=true and RandomizedDelaySec=15m. uupd itself wraps bootc/rpm-ostree + system and user Flatpaks + Homebrew.
facts.evidence: aurora system_files/shared/usr/lib/systemd/system-preset/89-aurora.preset contains `enable uupd.timer`. ublue-os/uupd repo root ships uupd.service, uupd.timer, uupd-manual.service (contents captured in snippets). uupd is installed from the ublue-os COPR in 01-packages.sh COPR_UBLUE_OS_PACKAGES.
facts.impact: Fleet update control = mask/override uupd.timer, not rpm-ostreed-automatic.timer. To pin the whole fleet to a schedule you control, ship a drop-in overriding uupd.timer's OnCalendar, or disable uupd.timer and drive `systemctl start uupd-manual.service` from your own orchestration.

facts.claim: rpm-ostreed-automatic is present but only as a fallback path and is set to `AutomaticUpdatePolicy=stage`; the shipped ujust `update` recipe explicitly prefers uupd.service when uupd.timer exists.
facts.evidence: aurora system_files/shared/etc/rpm-ostreed.conf: `[Daemon]` / `AutomaticUpdatePolicy=stage`. get-aurora-dev/common .../just/update.just: `if systemctl cat -- uupd.timer &> /dev/null; then SERVICE="uupd.service"; else SERVICE="rpm-ostreed-automatic.service"; fi`.
facts.impact: Don't configure rpm-ostreed-automatic.timer expecting it to be the driver — it isn't on this image.

facts.claim: Signing is cosign with a long-lived ECDSA P-256 key (keyless/Fulcio is explicitly disabled: COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL=false, --use-signing-config=false), signed on the digest, using the OLD sigstore bundle format because rpm-ostree/containers-libs cannot read the new one.
facts.evidence: ublue-os/aurora .github/workflows/reusable-build.yml, "Sign container image" step: `cosign sign -y --new-bundle-format=false --use-signing-config=false --key env://COSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY ${IMAGE_REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}@${DIGEST}` with comment referencing containers/container-libs#388 and coreos/rpm-ostree#5509.
facts.impact: If you sign your derived image, you MUST pass --new-bundle-format=false or bootc/rpm-ostree signature verification will fail on the client.

facts.claim: The on-disk enforcement config the image actually ships is: /etc/containers/policy.json with `"default": [{"type":"reject"}]`, a `ghcr.io/ublue-os` entry of type sigstoreSigned using **keyPaths** (plural — primary + backup key) at /usr/lib/pki/containers/ublue-os.pub and /usr/lib/pki/containers/ublue-os-backup.pub with signedIdentity matchRepository; plus /etc/containers/registries.d/ublue-os.yaml setting use-sigstore-attachments: true. Keys live under /usr/lib/pki/containers/, NOT /etc/pki/containers/ (that path is only used on the CI runner during build).
facts.evidence: get-aurora-dev/common system_files/shared/etc/containers/policy.json, .../registries.d/ublue-os.yaml, .../usr/lib/pki/containers/ublue-os.pub and ublue-os-backup.pub — all captured verbatim in snippets. The /etc/pki/containers path appears only in ublue-os/aurora .github/setup-runner-keys.sh, which configures the GitHub runner.
facts.impact: Copy this structure for your own namespace. Note the plural `keyPaths` — containers/image supports key rotation this way; use it so you can rotate without breaking the fleet.

facts.claim: ublue-os's primary cosign public key is identical in ublue-os/aurora/cosign.pub and get-aurora-dev/common .../ublue-os.pub (MFkwEwYHKoZIzj0CAQYIKoZIzj0DAQcDQgAEHLRpBfPRYiMl9wb7s6fx47PzzNWu3zyJgXhWEvxoOgwv9CpwjbvUwR9qHxNMWkJhuGE6cjDA2hpy1I6NbA+24Q==). The `cosign.pub` at the root of get-aurora-dev/common is a DIFFERENT key (…ELIik8ZM9ytEYEy1OWPs17Af7OEFH…) that signs the `common` build-context image, not ublue-os images.
facts.evidence: Byte-identical contents of repos/ublue-os/aurora/contents/cosign.pub and repos/get-aurora-dev/common/contents/system_files/shared/usr/lib/pki/containers/ublue-os.pub; repos/get-aurora-dev/common/contents/cosign.pub differs.
facts.impact: Grab the key from ublue-os/aurora/cosign.pub or the common repo's usr/lib/pki path. Do not grab get-aurora-dev/common's root cosign.pub by mistake.

facts.claim: `dnf5` is the correct way to install and remove packages in a Containerfile on this base today. rpm-ostree is NOT used for package operations anywhere in aurora's build, and the current image-template build.sh uses dnf5.
facts.evidence: ublue-os/aurora build_scripts/base/01-packages.sh uses `dnf5 remove`, `dnf5 distro-sync`, `dnf5 versionlock add`, `dnf -y install`, `dnf -y swap`, `dnf -y remove` — no rpm-ostree invocation. ublue-os/image-template build_files/build.sh: `dnf5 install -y tmux`.
facts.impact: Use `dnf5 install -y` / `dnf5 remove -y`. rpm-ostree only appears in the runtime ujust update fallback path for non-composefs deployments.

facts.claim: Aurora version-locks packages during build, and those locks persist into the image you derive from. Locked: `qt6-*`, `plasma-desktop`, `plasma-setup`, and the 12 mesa/intel/libva/libheif override packages.
facts.evidence: 01-packages.sh: `dnf versionlock add "qt6-*" "plasma-desktop"` (comment: "Prevent partial upgrading, major kde version updates black screened — https://github.com/ublue-os/aurora/issues/1227"); `dnf5 versionlock add "${OVERRIDES[@]}"`; `dnf versionlock add plasma-setup`.
facts.impact: A `dnf5 install` in your layer that needs a newer qt6-* or mesa will fail or silently skip. If you hit this, `dnf5 versionlock delete <pkg>` deliberately and document why — do not blanket-clear the locks.

facts.claim: Third-party repos (fedora-multimedia, tailscale, all COPRs, RPM Fusion, fedora-cisco-openh264) are shipped into /etc/yum.repos.d but set enabled=0 at the end of the build.
facts.evidence: build_scripts/base/17-cleanup.sh loops `sed -i 's@enabled=1@enabled=0@g'` over fedora-multimedia, tailscale, fedora-cisco-openh264, terra*, _copr:*, rpmfusion-*, fedora-coreos-pool. build_scripts/shared/build-prep.sh rsyncs build_files/shared/usr/share/dnf5/repos.d into /.
facts.impact: In your derived Containerfile you must use `dnf5 install --enablerepo=fedora-multimedia ...` or `--from-repo=...` for anything outside base Fedora. A plain `dnf5 install` will only see the Fedora repos.

facts.claim: GHCR retention will delete the digest you pin. aurora runs a weekly cleanup (Sundays 00:15 UTC) that deletes images older than 90 days, keeping only the 7 most recent tagged and 7 untagged manifests, with delete-orphaned-images: true.
facts.evidence: ublue-os/aurora .github/workflows/clean.yml: `dataaxiom/ghcr-cleanup-action` with `older-than: 90 days`, `keep-n-tagged: 7`, `keep-n-untagged: 7`, `delete-orphaned-images: true`, packages: aurora,aurora-dx,aurora-nvidia-open,aurora-dx-nvidia-open.
facts.impact: A pinned FROM digest is guaranteed to stop resolving within ~90 days (sooner if >7 stable builds land, which happens in under 2 months at weekly cadence). You must either mirror the base into your own registry or automate the digest bump (Renovate does this — aurora itself uses renovate.json5 and image-template pins its base by digest with a Renovate bot commit).

facts.claim: The current recommended template repo is ublue-os/image-template (last commit 1dd3b656c4eb99dea9fbf9bd8210a754bd94adab, 2026-09-04). Its README states: "This template is the recommended way to make customizations to any image published by the Universal Blue Project" and lists `ghcr.io/ublue-os/aurora:stable` as a base image option. Its Containerfile pins its default base by digest.
facts.evidence: repos/ublue-os/image-template README.md and Containerfile (`FROM ghcr.io/ublue-os/bazzite:stable@sha256:9556db65991d57a03a7dc18e4ba28a686d8bcdcd6b61235aa69c8267bb22ff76`, with `# FROM ghcr.io/ublue-os/aurora:stable` listed as an alternative).
facts.impact: Start from this template. Digest-pinning is already the template's own convention, which validates the pin-by-digest plan.

facts.claim: image-template's build workflow (.github/workflows/build.yml) runs, in order: checkout (pinned SHA) → ublue-os/remove-unwanted-software (free disk) → install just → `just check` (syntax) → `just image_name` → `just generate-default-tag` → lowercase registry/image → `just build` → `just ostree-rechunk` (chunkah offered as a commented alternative) → `just generate-build-tags` → `just tag-images` → docker/login-action to ghcr.io → `podman push` each alias tag (capturing /tmp/digestfile) → install cosign v3.1.2 → `cosign sign` on the digest. Triggers: pull_request to main, daily cron '05 10 * * *', push to main (paths-ignore **/README.md), and workflow_dispatch. Login/push/sign are all gated on `github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == refs/heads/<default_branch>`. Permissions: contents: read, packages: write, id-token: write. Runner: ubuntu-26.04.
facts.evidence: ublue-os/image-template .github/workflows/build.yml, read in full.
facts.impact: This is the skeleton to copy. Note there is no SBOM, no attestation and no secureboot check in the template (aurora's own reusable-build.yml adds syft SBOM, a secureboot check, and an ephemeral 'staging' pre-push so a push can never land unsigned). For a fleet, port aurora's ephemeral-tag-then-sign-then-push pattern — it exists specifically to stop unsigned images being published on CI flakes (containers/podman#27796).

facts.claim: image-template does NOT ship any policy.json or registries.d config for your own namespace. A derived image published to ghcr.io/<you> falls through policy.json's `"": [{"type":"insecureAcceptAnything"}]` docker entry, so `bootc switch --enforce-container-sigpolicy ghcr.io/<you>/<image>` will succeed without ever checking a signature.
facts.evidence: repos/ublue-os/image-template git tree contains only system_files/etc/.gitkeep and system_files/usr/.gitkeep — no containers/ config; README Step 2 covers generating the cosign key and the SIGNING_SECRET, but never mentions installing the public key or a policy entry into the image. get-aurora-dev/common policy.json has `"docker": { ... "": [{"type": "insecureAcceptAnything"}] }`.
facts.impact: This is the single biggest gap for a signature-enforcing fleet. You must add your own /usr/lib/pki/containers/<you>.pub, a policy.json transports.docker["ghcr.io/<you>"] sigstoreSigned entry, and a registries.d yaml with use-sigstore-attachments: true — inside your own image — or enforcement is cosmetic. snippets.name: Keep signature enforcement working for YOUR derived namespace (add to your build.sh)
snippets.code:
#!/usr/bin/bash
set -eoux pipefail

MY_NS="ghcr.io/YOURORG"
MY_KEY="/usr/lib/pki/containers/ghcr.io-YOURORG.pub"

# 1. Ship your cosign public key alongside ublue's (repo root cosign.pub -> system_files)
install -Dm0644 /ctx/system_files/usr/lib/pki/containers/ghcr.io-YOURORG.pub "${MY_KEY}"

# 2. Tell containers/image to look for sigstore attachments on your namespace
mkdir -p /etc/containers/registries.d
cat > /etc/containers/registries.d/YOURORG.yaml <<EOF
docker:
  ${MY_NS}:
    use-sigstore-attachments: true
EOF

# 3. Add a sigstoreSigned entry for your namespace WITHOUT clobbering ublue's.
#    keyPaths (plural) so you can rotate keys without breaking the fleet.
jq --arg ns "${MY_NS}" --arg key "${MY_KEY}" '
  .transports.docker[$ns] = [
    {
      "type": "sigstoreSigned",
      "keyPaths": [ $key ],
      "signedIdentity": { "type": "matchRepository" }
    }
  ]' /etc/containers/policy.json > /etc/containers/policy.json.tmp \
  && mv /etc/containers/policy.json.tmp /etc/containers/policy.json

snippets.name: How ublue signs (ublue-os/aurora reusable-build.yml, verbatim) — note --new-bundle-format=false
snippets.code:
- name: Install Cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@6f9f17788090df1f26f669e9d70d6ae9567deba6 # v4.1.2
        # be careful when upgrading major versions
        with:
          cosign-release: 'v3.1.3'

      - name: Sign container image
        if: inputs.publish
        env:
          DIGEST: ${{ steps.pre-push.outputs.digest }}
          COSIGN_EXPERIMENTAL: false
          COSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY: ${{ secrets.SIGNING_SECRET }}
          IMAGE_NAME: ${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          # use old bundle format, so we can use newer cosign 3.X.X instead of 2.X.X
          # https://github.com/containers/container-libs/issues/388
          # https://github.com/coreos/rpm-ostree/issues/5509
          cosign sign -y --new-bundle-format=false --use-signing-config=false --key env://COSIGN_PRIVATE_KEY ${IMAGE_REGISTRY}/${IMAGE_NAME}@${DIGEST}

[Unit]
Description=Auto Update System Timer For Universal Blue
Wants=network-online.target

[Timer]
# Run daily at 4:00 AM
OnCalendar=*-*-* 04:00:00

# If the system was off/suspended at 4:00 AM, trigger immediately on resume/boot
Persistent=true

# Wait up to 15 minutes after triggering and Spreads the load on update servers (thundering herd protection).

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target

gotchas: `stable-daily` is a legacy alias for `stable`, not a faster channel. The Justfile comment says so in plain English and both tags resolve to the same digest today. Any plan that treats stable-daily as a distinct cadence is wrong.
There is no `lts` and no `gts` tag on ghcr.io/ublue-os/aurora — those requests 404. LTS is a Bluefin/CentOS-bootc thing. Only stable, latest, testing exist.
`ghcr.io/ublue-os/aurora:stable` is x86_64 only — a single image manifest, not a multi-arch index. aarch64 is explicitly commented out of the build matrix. No arm64 fleet members.

Your pinned FROM digest has a hard expiry. clean.yml deletes GHCR manifests older than 90 days and keeps only the 7 most recent tagged manifests. At weekly stable cadence that is under two months. Either automate the bump with Renovate (ublue does exactly this) or mirror the base into a registry you control — for a fleet that must not break, mirror.

Fedora 45 is coming. `main` already pins quay.io/fedora-ostree-desktops/kinoite:45 and `:testing` is already 45.20260920.5. `:stable` and `:latest` still build from the `stable-f44` branch. The F44→F45 stable rebase will land as an ordinary `:stable` bump with no separate tag warning you. Gate it.

The build version-locks qt6-*, plasma-desktop, plasma-setup, and 12 mesa/intel/libva/libheif packages. A `dnf5 install` in your layer that wants a newer version of any of them will fail or skip. The qt6/plasma lock exists because partial KDE upgrades black-screened the desktop (ublue-os/aurora#1227) — do not clear it casually.

All third-party repos (fedora-multimedia, tailscale, every COPR, RPM Fusion, openh264) are shipped with enabled=0. `dnf5 install <pkg>` in a derived Containerfile only sees base Fedora. You need --enablerepo= or --from-repo=.

Signing must use `--new-bundle-format=false`. cosign 3.x defaults to the new bundle format, which rpm-ostree and containers/image cannot read (containers/container-libs#388, coreos/rpm-ostree#5509). Get this wrong and verification fails on every client with a confusing error.
ublue's policy.json uses `keyPaths` (plural) with a primary and a backup key. If you copy the pattern but write `keyPath` (singular) with one key, you lose the ability to rotate without a flag-day.

The public keys live at /usr/lib/pki/containers/, not /etc/pki/containers/. The /etc path appears only in .github/setup-runner-keys.sh, which configures the CI runner during the build — copying that script's paths into your image puts the keys where policy.json is not looking.

`quay.expires-after=4w` is a label on the :stable image inherited from the Fedora Kinoite base. It is a Quay-only mechanism and has no effect on GHCR — do not confuse it with the real 90-day GHCR cleanup.

rpm-ostreed.conf sets AutomaticUpdatePolicy=stage, which looks like the update mechanism but is not. uupd.timer is preset-enabled and is what actually runs. Configuring rpm-ostreed-automatic.timer will silently do nothing useful.
Aurora ships /etc/uupd/config.json with the distrobox module disabled. If you rely on uupd to refresh distrobox containers, it won't.

uupd runs a hardware/battery check by default; uupd-manual.service is the variant with --hw-check=false. If you drive updates from an orchestrator on laptops, you probably want uupd-manual.service, not uupd.service.
blockers: ublue-os/image-template — the officially recommended template — does NOT wire up signature enforcement for your own namespace. It ships no policy.json and no registries.d entry, and its README's signing section stops at 'put cosign.key in SIGNING_SECRET'. The base image's policy.json ends with a docker `"": [{"type":"insecureAcceptAnything"}]` catch-all, so `bootc switch --enforce-container-sigpolicy ghcr.io/<you>/<image>` will SUCCEED against your derived image while verifying nothing. If the plan says 'derive from aurora and signature enforcement keeps working', that premise is false as written — you must add your own key under /usr/lib/pki/containers/, your own registries.d yaml, and your own transports.docker["ghcr.io/<you>"] sigstoreSigned entry inside the image. Snippet provided.

area: bootc (containers/bootc) image lifecycle: upgrade/switch/rollback, status JSON, greenboot, signature enforcement, bootc-image-builder, lint, QEMU testing — as of 2026-09-20

facts.claim: `bootc upgrade` fetches the tracked image and stages it as an A/B deployment; it does not change the running system. The staged update is finalized at shutdown by `ostree-finalize-staged.service`. `--apply` reboots immediately; `--check` only pulls manifest+config metadata (kilobytes) to test for an update.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/docs/src/man/bootc-upgrade.8.md — "This does not affect the running system; updates operate in an \"A/B\" style by default. A queued update is visible as `staged` in `bootc status`." ... "Currently by default, the update will be applied at shutdown time via `ostree-finalize-staged.service`."
facts.impact: CI can stage without rebooting: `bootc upgrade --download-only`, verify `.status.staged`, then `bootc upgrade --from-downloaded --apply` in a maintenance window.

facts.claim: `bootc switch <TARGET>` is semantically identical to `bootc upgrade` except it also changes the tracked image reference; /etc and /var are preserved. Digest-pinned switches make `bootc upgrade` a permanent no-op, so with digests every update must be a `switch`.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/docs/src/upgrades.md — "`bootc switch` has the same effect as `bootc upgrade`; there is no semantic difference between the two other than changing the container image being tracked. This will preserve existing state in `/etc` and `/var`". Man page: "It is also supported to provide explicit digests ... When you do this, `bootc upgrade` will always be a no-op."
facts.impact: If we pin by digest in CI (recommended for reproducibility), the update agent must issue `bootc switch`, not `bootc upgrade`; a `bootc-fetch-apply-updates.timer` will do nothing.

facts.claim: New flags exist for staged/controlled rollout: `--download-only` stages without finalizing, `--from-downloaded` unlocks it, `bootc status --verbose` shows `Download-only: yes/no`, and the JSON BootEntry carries `downloadOnly: bool`. A reboot before applying discards the staged deployment (cached layers are kept).
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/docs/src/upgrades.md ("Staged updates with `--download-only`" section) and host-v1.schema.json $defs.BootEntry.downloadOnly: "Whether this deployment is in download-only mode (prevented from automatic finalization on shutdown). This is set via --download-only on the CLI."
facts.impact: Gives us a download/verify/apply split without writing our own agent.

facts.claim: `bootc status --json` emits a Kubernetes-style object with apiVersion `org.containers.bootc/v1`, kind `BootcHost`, metadata.name `host`, plus `spec` and `status`. Top-level `status` keys: booted, staged, rollback, rollbackQueued, otherDeployments, readOnly, type, usrOverlay.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/crates/lib/src/spec.rs — `const API_VERSION: &str = "org.containers.bootc/v1"; const KIND: &str = "BootcHost"; pub(crate) const OBJECT_NAME: &str = "host";` and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/docs/src/host-v1.schema.json
facts.impact: CI can assert on apiVersion before parsing, so a future v2 fails loudly instead of silently.

facts.claim: The exact JSON path to the BOOTED image digest is `.status.booted.image.imageDigest` (string, e.g. `sha256:a0...`). Sibling paths: image ref `.status.booted.image.image.image`, transport `.status.booted.image.image.transport`, signature mode `.status.booted.image.image.signature`, version label `.status.booted.image.version`, build timestamp `.status.booted.image.timestamp`, arch `.status.booted.image.architecture`, ostree commit `.status.booted.ostree.checksum`. Note the double nesting: BootEntry.image is an ImageStatus, and ImageStatus.image is an ImageReference whose own `.image` is the ref string.
facts.evidence: host-v1.schema.json: $defs.HostStatus.booted -> $defs.BootEntry; BootEntry.image -> $defs.ImageStatus; ImageStatus.imageDigest = {"description": "The digest of the fetched image (e.g. sha256:a0...);", "type": "string"}, required: [image, imageDigest, architecture]; ImageStatus.image -> $defs.ImageReference {image, transport, signature}
facts.impact: This is the field we gate CI on. The `.image.image.image` triple is the single most common parsing bug — write the jq once and test it.

facts.claim: `status.booted` is null on a non-bootc host; that is the documented way to detect a bootc system. greenboot upstream itself does exactly this.
facts.evidence: bootc-status.8.md: "Invoke e.g. `bootc status --json`, and check if `status.booted` is not `null`." Corroborated by https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fedora-iot/greenboot-rs/main/src/lib/handler.rs which runs `bootc status --booted --json` and walks `json.get("status").get("booted").get("image")`.
facts.impact: Same probe works for 'is this even a bootc box' in CI preflight.

facts.claim: `--format-version` currently accepts 0 or 1 and both mean the same schema; `--booted` restricts output to the booted deployment. Do not parse `--format=humanreadable`.
facts.evidence: bootc-status.8.md OPTIONS: "--format-version=FORMAT_VERSION  The desired format version. There is currently one supported version, which is exposed as both `0` and `1`." and "Do not attempt to explicitly parse the output of `--format=humanreadable` as it will very likely change over time."
facts.impact: Pass `--format-version=1` explicitly in CI so a future v2 default flip does not silently change our parse.

facts.claim: `bootc rollback` only reorders bootloader entries: the `rollback` deployment is queued for next boot and the current becomes rollback. Any staged upgrade is DISCARDED. It emits a journal message with MESSAGE_ID=26f3b1eb24464d12aa5e7b544a6b5468.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/docs/src/man/bootc-rollback.8.md
facts.impact: Detect rollbacks in fleet telemetry by that MESSAGE_ID rather than scraping text.

facts.claim: Rollback does NOT carry /etc changes back. Files in /etc revert to the previous deployment's state, because rollback reorders existing deployments and the 3-way /etc merge only happens when a deployment is created.
facts.evidence: bootc-rollback.8.md: "any changes made to files in the `/etc` directory won't carry over to the rolled-back deployment. The `/etc` files will revert to their state from that previous deployment instead. This is because `bootc rollback` just reorders the existing deployments."
facts.impact: Anything we write to /etc post-deploy (agent enrollment, certs) is lost on rollback. Put that state in /var or bake it into the image.

facts.claim: Deployments live at /ostree/deploy/$stateroot/deploy/$checksum.$serial, with shared /var at /ostree/deploy/$stateroot/var. `bootc install` always uses the stateroot named `default`; bootc does not yet expose stateroots.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ostreedev/ostree/main/docs/deployment.md ("A deployment is physically located at a path of the form /ostree/deploy/$stateroot/deploy/$checksum") and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/docs/src/filesystem-sysroot.md ("The `stateroot` used by `bootc install` is just named `default`.")
facts.impact: Hard-code /ostree/deploy/default/ in any disk-inspection tooling; it's stable today.

facts.claim: By default exactly TWO deployments are retained: the new one and the booted/merge one. Everything else for that stateroot is garbage collected. bootc's staged finalization passes only NO_CLEAN — no RETAIN/RETAIN_PENDING/RETAIN_ROLLBACK flag — so the libostree default applies. Deployments explicitly pinned (`ostree admin pin`) are exempt and surface in `.status.otherDeployments` with `pinned: true`.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ostreedev/ostree/main/src/libostree/ostree-sysroot.c doc comment: "Prepend @new_deployment to the list of deployments, commit, and cleanup. By default, all other deployments for the given @osname except the merge deployment and the booted deployment will be garbage collected." Retention loop: `if (retain || ostree_deployment_is_pinned (deployment) || !osname_matches || ...)`. bootc call site: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ostreedev/ostree/main/src/libostree/ostree-sysroot-deploy.c line ~4148 `OstreeSysrootSimpleWriteDeploymentFlags flags = OSTREE_SYSROOT_SIMPLE_WRITE_DEPLOYMENT_FLAGS_NO_CLEAN;` with comment "we always use NO_CLEAN to avoid adding more latency at shutdown".
facts.impact: There is exactly ONE rollback target. You cannot roll back two versions. If we want an N-2 escape hatch we must `ostree admin pin` a known-good deployment ourselves.

facts.claim: greenboot health-check directories are exactly: /etc/greenboot/check/required.d (failure => boot declared RED), /etc/greenboot/check/wanted.d (failure tolerated), /etc/greenboot/green.d (run after success), /etc/greenboot/red.d (run after failure). Distro-shipped checks live read-only under /usr/lib/greenboot/check/{required.d,wanted.d}.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fedora-iot/greenboot-rs/main/README.md (Usage > Health checks with bash scripts, incl. the literal directory tree) and the identical text in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fedora-iot/greenboot/main/README.md
facts.impact: Our health checks go in /etc/greenboot/check/required.d as executable shell scripts; mode 0755 matters.

facts.claim: The automatic-rollback retry count is GREENBOOT_MAX_BOOT_ATTEMPTS in /etc/greenboot/greenboot.conf, default 3. The shipped config file sets it to 3, and the code falls back to 3 when the key is absent.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fedora-iot/greenboot-rs/main/etc/greenboot/greenboot.conf contains literally `GREENBOOT_MAX_BOOT_ATTEMPTS=3`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fedora-iot/greenboot-rs/main/src/main.rs: `Err(_) => { log::debug!("GREENBOOT_MAX_BOOT_ATTEMPTS not found in config using default value : 3"); 3_u16 }`
facts.impact: 3 failed boots => rollback. To make CI fail fast set it to 1. The file is %config(noreplace), so a derived image should ship its own copy.

facts.claim: The GRUB mechanism: greenboot sets the `boot_counter` grubenv variable to GREENBOOT_MAX_BOOT_ATTEMPTS when an update is staged. GRUB's 08_greenboot.cfg decrements boot_counter on each boot while boot_success=0; when it hits 0 or -1 it sets `default=1` (the rollback entry) and pins boot_counter=-1. On a healthy boot greenboot sets boot_success=1 and UNSETS boot_counter. grubenv is /boot/grub2/grubenv, manipulated with `grub2-editenv`.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fedora-iot/greenboot-rs/main/grub2/08_greenboot.cfg (verbatim, see snippet) and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fedora-iot/greenboot-rs/main/src/lib/grub.rs: `static GRUB_PATH: &str = "/boot/grub2/grubenv";` with get/set/unset_boot_counter and `set_boot_status(true)` doing `set_grub_var("boot_success", 1)` + `unset_boot_counter()`.
facts.impact: `grub2-editenv /boot/grub2/grubenv list` is the one-liner to assert rollback state in a test VM. The cfg is installed to /usr/lib/bootupd/grub2-static/configs.d/08_greenboot.cfg, i.e. it depends on bootupd static GRUB configs — it will not work on a UKI/systemd-boot image.

facts.claim: greenboot-rs performs the actual rollback by shelling out to `bootc rollback` on bootc systems (and `rpm-ostree rollback` on rpm-ostree systems), and it refuses to roll back in Normal mode unless boot_counter has reached 0 — if boot_counter is unset it bails with "manual intervention required".
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fedora-iot/greenboot-rs/main/src/lib/handler.rs: `pub fn handle_rollback(mode: RollbackMode)`, `None => bail!("System is unhealthy but boot_counter is not set, manual intervention required")`, `Some(counter) if counter > 0 => bail!("Rollback not initiated as boot_counter is {}", counter)`, then `Command::new(deployment_cmd).arg("rollback")` where deployment_cmd is "bootc" or "rpm-ostree".
facts.impact: If boot_counter is never set (e.g. non-GRUB boot path), greenboot detects RED but will NOT roll back. Our tests must assert boot_counter is being set, not just that health checks run.

facts.claim: The shell greenboot is DEPRECATED in favor of greenboot-rs. RPM name stays `greenboot`; versions >= 0.16.0 are built from greenboot-rs. Unit names changed: the rs version ships only greenboot-healthcheck.service, greenboot-set-rollback-trigger.service and greenboot-success.target — the old greenboot-grub2-set-counter / greenboot-grub2-set-success / redboot-* / greenboot-rpm-ostree-grub2-check-fallback units are gone.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fedora-iot/greenboot/main/README.md deprecation banner: "The rpm package name remains `greenboot`. Versions **0.16.0 and above** are built from the `greenboot-rs` source code." Unit list from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fedora-iot/greenboot-rs/main/greenboot-rs.spec %files section (Version: 0.16.4).
facts.impact: Any `systemctl enable greenboot-grub2-set-counter ...` copy-pasted from older blog posts will fail on current images. Enable greenboot-healthcheck.service only.

facts.claim: greenboot is NOT preinstalled on Fedora bootc standard / minimal / minimal-plus images, and is NOT in Universal Blue's base image. It IS preinstalled on the Fedora bootc IoT variant. It must be explicitly `dnf install`ed in a derived Containerfile.
facts.evidence: https://gitlab.com/fedora/bootc/base-images/-/raw/main/iot/manifest.yaml contains `- greenboot` and `- greenboot-default-health-checks`; the same grep over standard/manifest.yaml and minimal-plus/manifest.yaml returns nothing. ublue-os/main packages.json has no greenboot entry and its Containerfile has no greenboot reference (GitHub tree API over ublue-os/main, ublue-os/bluefin and ublue-os/aurora returns zero greenboot paths).
facts.impact: Directly contradicts the common claim that greenboot ships on Universal Blue. We must add it ourselves. (ublue-os/bazzite is the exception — it ships an /etc/greenboot/greenboot.conf override, so greenboot arrives there via some other path.)

facts.claim: bootc honors the standard /etc/containers/policy.json via containers/image, and the upstream default policy is `{"default": [{"type": "insecureAcceptAnything"}]}` — i.e. unsigned images are accepted out of the box. bootc upstream explicitly states this is not a bug in bootc.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/docs/src/security.md: "bootc honors the default `/etc/containers/policy.json` when fetching images. The upstream default at the time of this writing does not require signatures for generic images. It is not a vulnerability in bootc that signatures are not required by default." Default file: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/image/main/default-policy.json
facts.impact: Signature enforcement is entirely on us; shipping a policy.json in the image is mandatory.

facts.claim: Signature enforcement at update time is two-part: (a) a restrictive policy.json, and (b) the deployment's stored sigverify mode must be `containerPolicy`. The mode is set by `bootc install ... --enforce-container-sigpolicy` or `bootc switch --enforce-container-sigpolicy`, persists in the ostree origin as `ostree-image-signed:`, and surfaces as `.status.booted.image.image.signature == "containerPolicy"`. Without it the mode is ContainerPolicyAllowInsecure (`ostree-unverified-image:`), which defers to whatever policy.json says including a permissive default.
facts.evidence: install.rs: "This is the inverse of the previous `--target-no-signature-verification` (which is now a no-op). Enabling this option enforces that `containers-policy.json` ... includes a default policy which requires signatures." spec.rs ImageSignature: ContainerPolicy = "Fetches will defer to the `containers-policy.json`, but we make a best effort to reject `default: insecureAcceptAnything` policy." ostree-ext/src/container/mod.rs: `"ostree-image-signed" => Ok(Self::ContainerPolicy), "ostree-unverified-image" => Ok(Self::ContainerPolicyAllowInsecure)`
facts.impact: THE gate for CI: assert `.status.booted.image.image.signature == "containerPolicy"`. If it's absent/null, signature enforcement is off regardless of how good policy.json is.

facts.claim: With ContainerPolicy set, bootc hard-errors before pulling if policy.json's default is a single insecureAcceptAnything entry, with the message "containers-policy.json specifies a default of `insecureAcceptAnything`; refusing usage". This check runs both in prepare_internal (manifest fetch) and in the base-layer fetch.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/crates/ostree-ext/src/container/store.rs lines ~942-956 and ~1048-1054; check implemented in crates/ostree-ext/src/container/skopeo.rs `container_policy_is_default_insecure()` which matches `default.split_first() => v.ty == INSECURE_ACCEPT_ANYTHING`.
facts.impact: Cheap smoke test: with enforcement on, deliberately ship the stock permissive policy and assert bootc upgrade fails with that exact string.

facts.claim: sigstoreSigned with a cosign public key requires `use-sigstore-attachments: true` in containers-registries.d(5) for the relevant scope, otherwise the signature attachment is never fetched and verification cannot succeed. Built-in default is that sigstore attachments are NOT read.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/image/main/docs/containers-policy.json.5.md: "To use this with images hosted on image registries, the `use-sigstore-attachments` option needs to be enabled for the relevant registry or repository in the client's containers-registries.d(5)." https://raw.githubusercontent.com/containers/image/main/docs/containers-registries.d.5.md Built-in Defaults: "Sigstore attachments will not be read/written."
facts.impact: Answering the question directly: YES, `use-sigstore-attachments: true` is required. Forgetting it is the #1 cause of 'my signed image is rejected'.

facts.claim: cosign-created signatures only bind a repository, so `signedIdentity` must be `matchRepository` or `exactRepository` — and upstream warns this does NOT protect against substituting a signed image under an unexpected tag. Exactly one of keyPath/keyPaths/keyData/keyDatas/fulcio/pki must be present.
facts.evidence: containers-policy.json.5.md sigstoreSigned section: "Note that `cosign`-created signatures only contain a repository, so only `matchRepository` and `exactRepository` can be used to accept them (and that does not protect against substitution of a signed image with an unexpected tag)." and "Exactly one of `keyPath`, `keyPaths`, `keyData`, `keyDatas`, `fulcio` and `pki` must be present."
facts.impact: Tag-substitution is not covered by signing alone. Pin by digest (`bootc switch <repo>@sha256:...`) if we need that guarantee.

facts.claim: bootc-image-builder turns an OCI image into a qcow2 or ISO via a privileged podman run of quay.io/centos-bootc/bootc-image-builder:latest with /output (required), optional /store and /rpmmd volumes, the host container storage bind-mounted, and `--type`. Image types: ami, anaconda-iso, bootc-installer, gce, iso, qcow2, raw, vhd, vmdk, pxe-tar-xz. `--type` can be repeated; comma/space separated lists do NOT work.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osbuild/image-builder/main/bootc-image-builder/README.md (identical text to the archived osbuild/bootc-image-builder README) — Arguments section and Volumes table.
facts.impact: One invocation can emit qcow2+ISO in a single osbuild run by passing --type twice; saves half the CI time.

facts.claim: `--rootfs` overrides the root filesystem type; supported values ext4, xfs, btrfs. Fedora bootc images have NO default rootfs configured in the container, so `--rootfs` is mandatory for them; the README's plain CentOS stream9 example omits it. With btrfs, custom /var mountpoints are not supported at all — only / and /boot.
facts.evidence: bootc-image-builder README: "--rootfs string  Root filesystem type. If not given, the default configured in the source container image is used." / "Note that some images (like fedora) do not have a default root filesystem type. In this case adds the switch `--rootfs <type>`" / "if the `rootfs` is `btrfs`, no custom mountpoints are supported under `/var`."
facts.impact: Use `--rootfs xfs` (or ext4). Do not pick btrfs if we want a separate /var/data partition.

facts.claim: The build config is a Blueprint TOML or JSON mounted at /config.toml, customizations under a `customizations` object. Users: name (required), password, key, groups. Filesystem: array of {mountpoint, minsize}; only /, /boot and subdirectories of /var are allowed — /var itself cannot be a mountpoint and symlinked paths like /var/home, /var/run cannot. Root fs final size is max(configured minsize, 2x base container size). JSON config can be piped in with `--config -`. An image can embed a default config at /usr/lib/bootc-image-builder/config.{json,toml}.
facts.evidence: bootc-image-builder README sections "📝 Build config", "Users (`user`, array)", "Filesystems (`filesystem`, array)", "Allowed mountpoints and sizes".
facts.impact: The 2x-base-image floor means a `minsize = "10 GiB"` on / may silently become larger; do not assert exact partition sizes in tests.

facts.claim: For an installable ISO use `--type anaconda-iso` (unattended Anaconda installer that installs to the first disk found, built from RPMs). `--type bootc-installer` is a different, newer thing: the positional arg must be a container with Anaconda baked in and you must also pass `--bootc-installer-payload-ref`. Kickstart content goes under [customizations.installer.kickstart].contents; bootc-image-builder injects the `ostreecontainer` line itself, and adds nothing else — partitioning, network, lang are all on you.
facts.evidence: bootc-image-builder README "💾 Image types" table and "### Anaconda ISO (installer) options (`installer`, mapping)": "bootc-image-builder will automatically add the command that installs the container image (`ostreecontainer ...`), so this line or any line that conflicts with it should not be included. No other kickstart commands are added by bootc-image-builder in this case".
facts.impact: anaconda-iso is what we want for an installable ISO. Budget time for writing a complete kickstart — the minimal example in the README is genuinely the minimum.

facts.claim: `bootc container lint` is designed for `RUN bootc container lint` inside a build. It runs 16 lints today: 7 fatal and 9 warnings. Fatal ones named in source include var-run, bootc-kargs, kernel, baseimage-root, nonempty-boot, nonempty-run-tmp, runtime-deps; warnings include buildah-injected, etc-usretc, api-base-directories, baseimage-composefs, var-log, var-tmpfiles, sysusers, utf8. Some lints are gated to RootType::Running vs Alternative.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/crates/lib/src/lints.rs — `Lint::new_fatal` appears 7x, `Lint::new_warning` 9x; LintType docs: Fatal = "the system will not install or is effectively guaranteed to fail at runtime", Warning = "not a fatal problem, but something you likely want to fix".
facts.impact: `bootc container lint --fatal-warnings` in the Containerfile is a cheap CI gate. `--list` emits YAML but upstream explicitly forbids parsing it.

facts.claim: Exit codes: `bootc container lint` (and bootc generally) exits 0 on success and 1 on any error. A fatal lint produces `anyhow::bail!("Checks failed: {n}")`, which bootc's main prints as `error: ...` and exits 1. There is no distinct per-lint exit code. The only other non-error exit is CliExitStatus::PredicateFalse, also exit 1, used today by an internal SELinux-label predicate — not by lint.
facts.evidence: lints.rs: `if fatal > 0 { anyhow::bail!("Checks failed: {}", fatal) }`. crates/utils/src/lib.rs `run_main`: `if let Err(e) = f() { ... writeln!(stderr, "{}{:#}", "error: ".red(), e); std::process::exit(1); }`. crates/cli/src/main.rs: `CliExitStatus::PredicateFalse => std::process::exit(1)`.
facts.impact: CI can only distinguish pass/fail, not lint-failed vs crashed. If we need that, grep stderr for the literal `Checks failed:` prefix.

facts.claim: Booting a bootc qcow2 headless in QEMU is the standard upstream test method, and there is no cloud-init involved for qcow2 — credentials come from the bootc-image-builder config.toml user block, and the harness reaches the VM over SSH via user-mode networking hostfwd. Anaconda/kickstart is only for the ISO path.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osbuild/bootc-image-builder/main/test/test_build_disk.py: `from vmtest.vm import AWS_REGION, AWS, QEMU`; `def assert_disk_image_boots(image_type): with QEMU(image_type.img_path, arch=image_type.img_arch) as test_vm: test_vm.run("true", user=image_type.username, password=image_type.password) ... test_vm.run(["bootc", "status"], ...)`. Harness: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/osbuild/images/main/test/scripts/imgtestlib/vm.py `_gen_qemu_cmdline` (full x86_64 argv reproduced in snippets).
facts.impact: We can lift the upstream qemu argv verbatim: -nographic, -serial stdio, -snapshot, hostfwd SSH, QMP socket for boot-event waits. `vmtest` is pip-installable straight from the images repo (`vmtest @ git+https://github.com/osbuild/images.git`).

facts.claim: Boot-failure detection on the ostree backend is ostree-finalize-staged.service (shutdown) writing a stamp in /boot, detected on next boot by ostree-boot-complete.service, which then fails. The composefs backend has bootc-finalize-staged.service but NO boot-complete equivalent and does NOT configure GRUB boot-entry counting yet.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/docs/src/boot-failure-detection.md
facts.impact: Monitor ostree-boot-complete.service for 'the previous update failed to finalize'. If we ever move to composefs/UKI we lose greenboot's grub boot_counter rollback entirely.

facts.claim: `bootc switch --transport containers-storage <ref>` boots a locally built podman image without a registry round-trip; other supported transports are registry (default), oci, oci-archive, docker-daemon. For airgapped delivery, `skopeo copy docker://... oci:/path/myos.oci` then `bootc switch --transport oci /var/mnt/usb/myos.oci`.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/docs/src/booting-local-builds.md and docs/src/registries-and-offline.md
facts.impact: Lets CI test a locally built image on a live box in seconds; also the airgap story if we need it.

facts.claim: bootc has no --tls-verify flag; insecure registries must be configured globally via /etc/containers/registries.conf.d. Private registry auth for bootc specifically reads /etc/ostree/auth.json (not the usual containers auth path).
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bootc-dev/bootc/main/docs/src/registries-and-offline.md: "`bootc` has no such option" and "This is configured by placing an `auth.json` file at `/etc/ostree/auth.json`."
facts.impact: Our pull secret must land at /etc/ostree/auth.json in the image or via config management, or upgrades fail on a private registry even though podman works.

facts.claim: `bootc upgrade --tag <TAG>` exists to move to a different tag of the currently booted image without a full switch.
facts.evidence: bootc-upgrade.8.md OPTIONS: `**--tag**=*TAG*  Upgrade to a different tag of the currently booted image` with examples `bootc upgrade --tag v1.2`, `bootc upgrade --tag prod --check`.
facts.impact: Simpler than `switch` for promoting a host between channels on the same repo.

snippets.name: CI gate: parse booted image digest from bootc status --json
snippets.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

S=$(bootc status --booted --format=json --format-version=1)

# Fail loudly if the schema version ever changes.
[ "$(jq -r '.apiVersion' <<<"$S")" = "org.containers.bootc/v1" ] || { echo "unexpected bootc status apiVersion" >&2; exit 1; }
[ "$(jq -r '.kind'       <<<"$S")" = "BootcHost" ]               || { echo "unexpected bootc status kind" >&2; exit 1; }

# Not a bootc host at all?
jq -e '.status.booted != null' <<<"$S" >/dev/null || { echo "not a bootc system" >&2; exit 1; }

# THE field: booted image manifest digest, e.g. sha256:a0...
BOOTED_DIGEST=$(jq -er '.status.booted.image.imageDigest' <<<"$S")

# Siblings. Note the .image.image.image triple nesting -- BootEntry.image is an
# ImageStatus, ImageStatus.image is an ImageReference, and its .image is the ref string.
BOOTED_REF=$(jq -er   '.status.booted.image.image.image'     <<<"$S")
BOOTED_TRANSPORT=$(jq -er '.status.booted.image.image.transport' <<<"$S")
BOOTED_SIGMODE=$(jq -r  '.status.booted.image.image.signature // "none"' <<<"$S")
BOOTED_VERSION=$(jq -r  '.status.booted.image.version // ""'  <<<"$S")
OSTREE_CSUM=$(jq -r     '.status.booted.ostree.checksum // ""' <<<"$S")

# Signature enforcement gate: "containerPolicy" means policy.json is enforced.
# Anything else (null / "insecure" / {"ostreeRemote":...}) means it is NOT.
[ "$BOOTED_SIGMODE" = "containerPolicy" ] || { echo "SIGNATURE ENFORCEMENT OFF (signature=$BOOTED_SIGMODE)" >&2; exit 1; }

[ "$BOOTED_DIGEST" = "$EXPECTED_DIGEST" ] || { echo "digest mismatch: $BOOTED_DIGEST != $EXPECTED_DIGEST" >&2; exit 1; }

# Rollback target present? (there is only ever ONE)
jq -e '.status.rollback != null' <<<"$S" >/dev/null && \
  echo "rollback available: $(jq -r '.status.rollback.image.imageDigest' <<<"$S")"

# Note: --booted omits .status.staged. Drop --booted to inspect a staged update:
#   bootc status --format=json | jq -r '.status.staged.image.imageDigest, .status.staged.downloadOnly'

# greenboot support, aka boot counter and boot success reporting
# This will be installed via bootupd
insmod increment
# Check if boot_counter exists and boot_success=0 to activate this behavior.
if [ -n "${boot_counter}" -a "${boot_success}" = "0" ]; then
  # if countdown has ended, choose to boot rollback deployment,
  # i.e. default=1 on OSTree-based systems.
  if  [ "${boot_counter}" = "0" -o "${boot_counter}" = "-1" ]; then
    set default=1
    set boot_counter=-1
  # otherwise decrement boot_counter
  else
    decrement boot_counter
  fi
  save_env boot_counter
fi

# Reset boot_success for current boot
set boot_success=0
save_env boot_success

#!/usr/bin/bash

# Any non-zero exit here declares the boot RED.
# After GREENBOOT_MAX_BOOT_ATTEMPTS (default 3) failed boots, GRUB's
# boot_counter reaches 0, GRUB sets default=1, and greenboot runs `bootc rollback`.

systemctl is-active --quiet my-app.service

for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
  if curl -fsS --max-time 2 http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz >/dev/null; then
    exit 0
  fi
  sleep 2
done

echo "my-app did not become healthy within 60s" >&2
exit 1
