facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/sdk-api/docs/sdk-api-src/content/vsbackup/nf-vsbackup-createvssbackupcomponents.md — "This function is exported as CreateVssBackupComponentsInternal, but you should call CreateVssBackupComponents"; Library VssApi.lib, DLL VssApi.dll
facts.impact: This is why VSS from Go is hard, but not impossible — the export name is plain C-callable via LazyDLL, and the interface can be driven by hand-built vtable dispatch.

facts.claim: A pure-Go (no cgo) VSS requester exists and works: github.com/SmithOperatingSolutions/go-vss loads vssapi.dll with System32-only search and does manual MSVC-ABI vtable dispatch. It exposes Create/CreateSet/List/Attach/Delete plus snapshot FS()/Open()/Walk(). It requires an elevated (Administrators) process, is native-64-bit only (32-bit and WOW64 refused at startup), supports Win7/2008R2 → Win11/2025, and treats FAT32 as not snapshot-able.
facts.evidence: https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/SmithOperatingSolutions/go-vss — "Pure-Go (no cgo) Windows Volume Shadow Copy Service requester"; "VSS is a C++ vtable COM API with no type library; methods are invoked by vtable slot index with a hand-built MSVC ABI"; "the process must run elevated (Administrators)"
facts.impact: Answers item 3 affirmatively: VSS IS usable from a single static Go exe. Cost: UAC elevation + 64-bit-only + a third-party dep doing ABI tricks. Budget a fallback path.

facts.claim: The simpler locked-file approach is real: open with dwShareMode = FILE_SHARE_READ|FILE_SHARE_WRITE|FILE_SHARE_DELETE (0x1|0x2|0x4) and FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS (0x02000000), which "ensures that the calling process overrides file security checks when the process has SE_BACKUP_NAME and SE_RESTORE_NAME privileges" and is also required to get a handle to a directory.
facts.evidence: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MicrosoftDocs/sdk-api/docs/sdk-api-src/content/fileapi/nf-fileapi-createfilew.md — verbatim
facts.impact: This is the 80% answer and needs no VSS, no elevation for the user's own files, and no external process. It fails only where the owner opened the file with dwShareMode=0 (Outlook .pst/.ost, SQLite -wal in use, some accounting apps). Reserve VSS for that residue.

facts.claim: `netsh wlan export profile name="X" folder="C:\path" key=clear` writes WLANProfile XML in namespace https://www.microsoft.com/networking/WLAN/profile/v1; the cleartext PSK lands in MSM/security/sharedKey/keyMaterial with <keyType>passPhrase</keyType> and <protected>false</protected>.
facts.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/nativewifi/wlan-profileschema-schema (namespace quoted verbatim) + https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/nativewifi/wpa2-personal-profile-sample (sharedKey snippet quoted verbatim)
facts.impact: Parse with encoding/xml. Read <name>, SSIDConfig/SSID/name, MSM/security/authEncryption/{authentication,encryption}, sharedKey/{keyType,protected,keyMaterial}. That is exactly the set NetworkManager needs.

facts.claim: Windows authentication values map to NM key-mgmt as: WPA2PSK/WPAPSK → key-mgmt=wpa-psk; open + encryption none → no [wifi-security] section; WPA3SAE → key-mgmt=sae. NM keyfiles live in /etc/NetworkManager/system-connections/ and NM "will ignore files that are readable or writable by any user other than 'root'".
facts.evidence: https://networkmanager.dev/docs/api/latest/nm-settings-keyfile.html — file location and permission rule; section/key names [connection]/[wifi]/[wifi-security] with key-mgmt=wpa-psk and psk
facts.impact: Yes, the cleartext PSK converts cleanly to an NM keyfile. Emit files chmod 0600 root:root or NM silently ignores them — this is the #1 way this feature ships broken.

facts.claim: Installed-programs enumeration requires four registry roots: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall, HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall, HKCU\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall, HKCU\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall. Documented values include DisplayName, DisplayVersion, Publisher, InstallDate, InstallLocation, InstallSource, UninstallString, EstimatedSize, Comments, HelpLink.
facts.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/msi/uninstall-registry-key — "HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall" plus the value/property table quoted verbatim
facts.impact: Use golang.org/x/sys/windows/registry with registry.KEY_READ|registry.WOW64_64KEY and again with WOW64_32KEY (or just read the literal WOW6432Node path). Filter out entries with SystemComponent=1, empty DisplayName, or ParentKeyName set, else the list is 60% Windows updates and VC++ runtimes.

facts.claim: EnumPrinters(Flags, Name, Level, pPrinterEnum, cbBuf, pcbNeeded, pcReturned) in Winspool.drv (EnumPrintersW) with Flags = PRINTER_ENUM_LOCAL|PRINTER_ENUM_CONNECTIONS and Name=NULL "enumerates printers that are installed on the local machine ... physically attached ... as well as remote printers to which it has a network connection." Level 2 gives PRINTER_INFO_2 (pPrinterName, pPortName, pDriverName, pServerName, Attributes); Level 4 is fast (registry-only).
facts.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/printdocs/enumprinters — syntax, flags table and Remarks quoted verbatim
facts.impact: Callable from Go via LazyDLL("winspool.drv").NewProc("EnumPrintersW"). IMPORTANT: Level 2 does an OpenPrinter RPC per remote connection and "must wait for RPC to time out" on dead servers — call Level 4 first to get names, then Level 2 only for local printers.

facts.claim: Almost nothing about a Windows printer is portable to CUPS. The Windows driver (pDriverName, a .INF/GPD/PPD-in-disguise) has no Linux counterpart. CUPS has deprecated PPDs and drivers entirely: raw queues deprecated in CUPS 2.2 (2018), printer drivers in CUPS 2.3 (2019), with removal targeted for CUPS 3.0 in favour of IPP Everywhere / driverless and Printer Applications.
facts.evidence: https://openprinting.github.io/cups/drivers.html and https://wiki.debian.org/CUPSDriverlessPrinting
facts.impact: Migrate only: queue name, location/comment, default flag, and the network endpoint. A Standard TCP/IP port becomes socket://<ip>:9100 or ipp://<ip>/ipp/print; on modern CUPS the right move is to emit `lpadmin -p NAME -E -v ipp://<ip>/ipp/print -m everywhere`. USB-attached printers: emit a note, not a config. Do not attempt driver translation.

facts.claim: Windows printer port details (IP, port number) are in the registry at HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Monitors\Standard TCP/IP Port\Ports\<PortName> with values HostName, IPAddress, PortNumber, Protocol; queues themselves are under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Print\Printers\<QueueName>.
facts.evidence: Not verified against a primary source in this session — from prior knowledge of the Windows print subsystem layout.
facts.impact: EnumPrinters gives you pPortName (e.g. "IP_192.168.1.50") but not the IP. You need this registry read to build the CUPS device URI. Verify on a real machine before relying on it.

facts.claim: Chrome/Chromium user data dir on Windows is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data (Chromium: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Chromium\User Data); "Each profile is a subdirectory (often Default) within the user data directory", with additional profiles as Profile 1, Profile 2. Edge is %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\<Profile>.
facts.evidence: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/user_data_dir.md (verbatim paths); Edge path per https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/answers/questions/2392684/
facts.impact: Enumerate profile dirs by reading User Data\Local State JSON → profile.info_cache, rather than globbing, so you get the human names.

facts.claim: Per-profile Chromium files: Bookmarks (JSON, portable), History (SQLite, portable), Web Data (SQLite, autofill — encrypted fields not portable), Login Data (SQLite, passwords), and Cookies which since M96 lives in the profile's Network/ subdirectory (Default\Network\Cookies).
facts.evidence: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/HEAD/docs/user_data_dir.md and corroborating forensics sources; the Network/ relocation is widely documented

facts.claim: Chrome App-Bound Encryption shipped in Chrome 127 on Windows; the AES key in Local State is wrapped by the SYSTEM-privileged Elevation Service (IElevator) which verifies the caller is a legitimate signed chrome.exe, binding the key to the application binary on that machine. Ciphertext carries a v20 prefix and now covers cookies, passwords and payment data.
facts.evidence: https://security.googleblog.com/2024/07/improving-security-of-chrome-cookies-on-windows.html (title/date confirmed; body not retrievable by fetch) + https://github.com/xaitax/Chrome-App-Bound-Encryption-Decryption/blob/main/docs/RESEARCH.md + https://blog.elcomsoft.com/2026/01/browser-forensics-in-2026-app-bound-encryption-and-live-triage/
facts.impact: Confirms the premise: Chrome cookies are non-portable off-machine. Correction to the premise: passwords are v20 too, so it is ABE *and* DPAPI, not DPAPI alone.

facts.claim: Edge's equivalent is the ApplicationBoundEncryptionEnabled policy, "Supported versions: Windows ≥ 127". MS states: "Enabling this policy or leaving it unset binds the encryption keys used for local data storage to Microsoft Edge whenever possible." It names as a disable-only scenario: "Encrypted user data is expected to be fully portable between different computers".
facts.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/deployedge/microsoft-edge-browser-policies/applicationboundencryptionenabled — quoted verbatim
facts.impact: Microsoft itself documents that app-bound encryption is what makes Edge data non-portable between computers. Cite this to the user rather than arguing.

facts.claim: DPAPI is machine-bound by design: "Usually, the only user who can decrypt the data is a user with the same logon credentials as the user who encrypted the data. In addition, the encryption and decryption must be done on the same computer."
facts.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/dpapi/nf-dpapi-cryptunprotectdata — verbatim opening sentence
facts.impact: The one-sentence primary-source justification for 'passwords do not migrate'. Decrypt in-place on the source machine while the user is logged in, or not at all.

facts.claim: Firefox profiles on Windows: roaming data at %APPDATA%\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles, cache at %LOCALAPPDATA%\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles, with the index in %APPDATA%\Mozilla\Firefox\profiles.ini. Modern Firefox identifies installations by CityHash of the install directory recorded inside profiles.ini rather than a separate installs.ini.
facts.evidence: https://firefox-source-docs.mozilla.org/toolkit/profile/index.html — paths quoted; also mentions %APPDATA%\Mozilla\Firefox\Profile Groups for the Selectable Profile Service
facts.impact: Parse profiles.ini for [ProfileN] Path=/IsRelative=/Default= rather than globbing *.default-release. Copy only the roaming tree; the Local tree is cache.

facts.claim: Firefox is the one genuinely portable browser: places.sqlite holds bookmarks + history + downloads, cookies.sqlite holds cookies, logins.json + key4.db together hold passwords, cert9.db holds certificates, favicons.sqlite, formhistory.sqlite, permissions.sqlite, persdict.dat, prefs.js. Mozilla's guidance is to copy individual files with Firefox closed rather than restoring a whole profile folder.
facts.evidence: https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/profiles-where-firefox-stores-user-data and https://support.mozilla.org/en-US/kb/about-your-important-data-and-their-files
facts.impact: Firefox passwords DO migrate cross-machine (logins.json + key4.db travel together; no DPAPI binding unless a Primary Password is set). This is a real differentiator to tell the user about: Firefox → Firefox on Linux is a full migration; Chrome → anything is not.

facts.claim: `manage-bde -protectors -disable <drive> [-rebootcount <integer 0 - 15>]` — "protection of the operating system volume has been suspended and will resume after Windows has been restarted the number of times specified"; "Specify 0 to suspend protection indefinitely"; "If this parameter isn't specified, BitLocker protection automatically resumes after Windows is restarted." -rc is the abbreviation. -disable makes the key "available unsecured on drive"; no protectors are removed.
facts.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/manage-bde-protectors — syntax and parameter table quoted verbatim, plus example `manage-bde -protectors -disable C: -rc 3`
facts.impact: Your command is correct. -RebootCount 1 = survive exactly one reboot then auto-resume, which is precisely the one-shot-boot-to-USB semantics you want. Requires elevation.

facts.claim: BitLocker status is detectable programmatically via WMI namespace Root\CIMV2\Security\MicrosoftVolumeEncryption, class Win32_EncryptableVolume: ProtectionStatus 0=PROTECTION OFF, 1=PROTECTION ON, 2=PROTECTION UNKNOWN ("One potential cause is that the volume is in a locked state"); ConversionStatus 0=FULLY DECRYPTED,1=FULLY ENCRYPTED,2=ENCRYPTION IN PROGRESS,3=DECRYPTION IN PROGRESS,4/5=PAUSED. Methods GetProtectionStatus/GetConversionStatus give real-time values. Requires administrator privileges.
facts.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/secprov/win32-encryptablevolume — property tables and Security Considerations quoted verbatim
facts.impact: Query this before touching boot config. Note the doc's warning that the class property is a snapshot from instantiation — call the GetProtectionStatus METHOD, not the property, if you act on it.

facts.claim: `bcdedit /bootsequence <id> [...] [/addfirst|/addlast|/remove]` "sets the one-time boot sequence to be used by the boot manager." Applied to the firmware object, `Bcdedit /set {fwbootmgr} displayorder {bootmgr} /addfirst` is MS's own documented pattern for ordering UEFI firmware entries; {fwbootmgr} manipulations write through to NVRAM.
facts.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/drivers/devtest/bcdedit--bootsequence (verbatim) + https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-hardware/manufacture/desktop/bcd-system-store-settings-for-uefi ("Bcdedit /set {fwbootmgr} displayorder {bootmgr} /addfirst")
facts.impact: `bcdedit /set {fwbootmgr} bootsequence {GUID}` is the documented-by-composition way to set UEFI BootNext. MS does not document the exact {fwbootmgr} + bootsequence pairing on a single page — treat it as working-but-underdocumented.

facts.claim: `shutdown /fw`: "Combining this option with a shutdown option causes the next restart to go to the firmware user interface." `shutdown /a` "Combine with /fw to clear any pending boots to firmware." `/t xxx` default is 30s; "If the timeout period is greater than 0, the /f parameter is implied." Users need the "Shut down the system" user right.
facts.evidence: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/administration/windows-commands/shutdown — parameter table quoted verbatim
facts.impact: /fw goes to the FIRMWARE SETUP UI, not to your USB. It is NOT a one-time boot to a device — it is 'drop the user into BIOS setup'. `shutdown /r /fw /t 0` and `bcdedit bootsequence` are two different mechanisms; don't conflate them. /fw is the honest fallback when NVRAM manipulation fails, because it at least puts the user one menu away.

facts.claim: Writing a bootable USB from Windows with no dependencies requires: opening \\.\PhysicalDriveN with GENERIC_READ|GENERIC_WRITE, FSCTL_LOCK_VOLUME + FSCTL_DISMOUNT_VOLUME on every child volume, IOCTL_DISK_CREATE_DISK / IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX to lay down GPT, formatting an ESP as FAT32, and sector-aligned WriteFile — all elevated, all destructive, all easy to get wrong on a machine you do not own.
facts.evidence: Synthesis of Win32 disk API surface; no single primary source read this session.
facts.impact: See blockers. The correct product decision is to not write the USB from Windows at all.

gotchas: FILE_ATTRIBUTE_RECALL_ON_OPEN (0x00040000) has the SAME numeric value as FILE_ATTRIBUTE_EA (0x00040000). MS documents both at 262144. Testing that bit from GetFileAttributesW is meaningless — it is only populated in directory-enumeration info classes. Use FindFirstFileW or GetFileInformationByHandleEx(FileIdBothDirectoryInfo), or just call CfGetPlaceholderStateFromFindData and stop hand-rolling bit tests.

FILE_ATTRIBUTE_OFFLINE alone is NOT a OneDrive signal — it is the legacy HSM/Remote Storage bit, and MS says "Applications should not arbitrarily change this attribute." Files On-Demand cloud-only files set RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS; some sync engines set OFFLINE too, some don't. Test RECALL_ON_DATA_ACCESS primarily and treat OFFLINE as a weak corroborator.

The only Microsoft page that tells apps how to handle placeholders (learn.microsoft.com/windows/compatibility/placeholder-files) is for the obsolete Windows 8.1 model and tells you to check IO_REPARSE_TAG_FILE_PLACEHOLDER (0x80000015), which no current machine uses. Ignore it; the live tag is IO_REPARSE_TAG_CLOUD 0x9000001A.

The honest hydration behaviour: do a metadata-only pass first (FindFirstFileW + CfGetPlaceholderStateFromFindData), sum the bytes of everything with PARTIALLY_ON_DISK set, and SHOW THE USER that number before copying anything. Then offer three choices: (a) skip cloud-only files and emit a manifest of what was skipped, (b) hydrate and copy, with the GB figure and a metered-connection warning, (c) skip and tell them to sign into OneDrive on the Linux side instead. Silently copying is the one thing you must not do — a cloud-only file read through normal CreateFile/ReadFile succeeds and hydrates, so a naive walker downloads the user's entire OneDrive without asking. Reading them with FILE_FLAG_OPEN_NO_RECALL is worse: it succeeds and gives you a file that is not the file.

A 2012–2018 laptop may well be running 32-bit Windows 10. go-vss refuses to start on 32-bit and under WOW64. If you ship a single static exe you almost certainly want to ship both amd64 and 386 builds, and have the 386 build degrade to backup-semantics-only with no VSS.

netsh wlan export profile writes the PSK in cleartext to disk. Write it to a directory you created with a restrictive DACL, and shred it after conversion. Do not stage it on the USB stick alongside the user's documents.

keyMaterial is not always a passphrase. If <keyType> is networkKey rather than passPhrase, the value is a 64-hex-char PMK, which NetworkManager also accepts as psk — but only if it is exactly 64 hex chars. Validate before writing, or NM will silently fail to associate.

Non-ASCII SSIDs: netsh may emit <hex>...</hex> under SSIDConfig/SSID instead of <name>. NM keyfile ssid= is a UTF-8 string. Decode the hex before writing or you will produce a connection that never matches.

EnumPrinters at Level 2 does an OpenPrinter RPC per remote connection and, per MS, "must wait for RPC to time out" against dead print servers. On a laptop that has been in three offices this can hang for minutes. Call Level 4 first (registry-only, returns immediately), then Level 2 only for entries you have already filtered to local.

Nothing about a Windows print driver survives the trip to CUPS, and CUPS is actively removing driver support (raw queues deprecated 2.2/2018, drivers 2.3/2019, removal targeted for 3.0). Migrate the IP and the queue name and nothing else. USB printers: report them, do not attempt to configure them.
Chrome's Cookies file moved into the profile's Network/ subdirectory around M96. Code that globs Default/Cookies finds nothing on any machine you will meet.

Firefox passwords DO migrate (logins.json + key4.db as a pair, same profile directory) while Chrome/Edge passwords do not. This asymmetry is worth surfacing in the product, not burying: it is a real reason to tell a user to switch to Firefox before migrating.

manage-bde, bcdedit, Win32_EncryptableVolume and VSS all require elevation. If the tool is not elevated the BitLocker/boot half of the feature set is simply unavailable — decide whether you relaunch with a UAC prompt or ship two modes, and do it deliberately rather than discovering it at runtime.

`shutdown /r /fw` and `bcdedit /set {fwbootmgr} bootsequence` are different mechanisms with different outcomes. /fw drops the user in the BIOS setup screen; bootsequence sets UEFI BootNext to boot a specific entry. Shipping /fw while describing it as 'boot to the USB' will generate support calls.

{fwbootmgr} bootsequence reliability is firmware-dependent on 2012–2018 hardware. Several OEM firmwares of that vintage ignore or clear BootNext, re-enumerate USB entries on every boot (so yesterday's GUID is stale), or reorder the boot list on their own. Always re-read `bcdedit /enum {fwbootmgr}` immediately before setting it, and always have the manual F12 instructions printed on screen as the real fallback.

Legacy BIOS/CSM machines from 2012–2014 have no {fwbootmgr} object at all. Detect UEFI vs BIOS first (the {fwbootmgr} enum failing is itself the signal) and do not attempt NVRAM manipulation on CSM boxes.
blockers: `vssadmin create shadow` does not exist on Windows 10/11 client SKUs. The current Microsoft vssadmin reference (updated 2026-09-08) lists exactly seven subcommands, all marked 'Client and Server', and `create shadow` is not among them — it survives only in archived Windows Server 2008/2012 R2 documentation. Any design step that shells out to it will fail on every target machine. Remove it.

`wmic shadowcopy call create` is dead on the newer half of the target fleet. WMIC is removed by default from new Windows 11 24H2 and 25H2 installs, is no longer available as a Feature on Demand, and the August 2026 preview update removes it from already-installed 24H2/25H2 machines. It still exists on Windows 10, so this is a fleet-split, not a total loss — but it cannot be the primary mechanism.

'Single static exe, no runtime dep' and 'use VSS' are in tension, though not fatally. There is no C-callable, COM-registered VSS entry point: CreateVssBackupComponents is exported as CreateVssBackupComponentsInternal and IVssBackupComponents is a C++ vtable interface with no type library. A pure-Go requester exists (github.com/SmithOperatingSolutions/go-vss, hand-built MSVC-ABI vtable dispatch) so the goal is achievable, but it costs a third-party dependency doing fragile ABI work, requires an elevated process, and refuses to run on 32-bit or WOW64. Recommended shape: backup-semantics + full sharing as the default path for ~95% of files, VSS as an opt-in escalation for the locked residue, and an honest 'these N files were in use and were skipped' manifest when VSS is unavailable.

Premise correction on item 7: App-Bound Encryption is not only about cookies. As of Chrome/Edge 127+ the v20 wrapping covers cookies, saved passwords and payment data, so 'ABE makes cookies non-portable and DPAPI makes passwords non-portable' understates it — passwords are protected by DPAPI *and* ABE. Microsoft says so directly for Edge: disabling the ApplicationBoundEncryptionEnabled policy is only for cases where 'Encrypted user data is expected to be fully portable between different computers'. The correct product position is: Chrome/Edge bookmarks and history migrate; cookies, passwords and payment data do not, full stop, and the user must use Chrome/Edge profile sync or export passwords by hand from chrome://password-manager before the wipe. Do not build a decryptor — the published techniques require injecting into or impersonating the signed browser binary, which is malware behaviour and will be flagged as such by Defender.

Item 10 as framed should be dropped rather than solved. Writing a bootable USB from Windows with no dependencies means: elevated open of \\.\PhysicalDriveN, FSCTL_LOCK_VOLUME/FSCTL_DISMOUNT_VOLUME on every child volume, IOCTL_DISK_CREATE_DISK + IOCTL_DISK_SET_DRIVE_LAYOUT_EX to write GPT, a hand-rolled FAT32 ESP, and sector-aligned raw writes — irreversibly destructive, on a machine you do not own, with no undo. You can avoid it entirely: the Linux target machine (or any second machine) creates its own install media with the tools it already has, and your Windows-side exe does only what it is good at — enumerate, stage a migration bundle to an ordinary external drive as plain files, and leave the boot media to someone else. If you must touch boot at all, stop at `bcdedit /set {fwbootmgr} bootsequence` against media the user already made.

facts.claim: Versions: astro 7.3.3 (2026-09-16); @astrojs/cloudflare 14.3.2 (2026-09-16), peerDeps astro ^7.2.0 + wrangler ^4.125.0; wrangler 4.135.0 (2026-09-18).

facts.claim: Assets are served first; the Worker runs only when no asset matches. BUT with compatibility_date >= 2025-04-01, navigation requests (Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate) never invoke the Worker — they fall to not_found_handling.

facts.claim: assets.run_worker_first accepts true or an array of glob patterns with ! negation, max 100 entries; negatives win.
facts.evidence: workers/static-assets/binding.mdx L95-127, incl. example "run_worker_first": ["/api/*", "!/api/docs/*"]

facts.claim: If you DO use the adapter (SSR), wrangler `main` is now the adapter entrypoint '@astrojs/cloudflare/entrypoints/server', not dist/_worker.js/index.js. Astro.locals.runtime is removed; use `import { env } from 'cloudflare:workers'`. astro dev/preview now run in workerd.
facts.evidence: cloudflare.mdx 'Upgrading to v13 and Astro 6' -> '### Changed: Wrangler entrypoint configuration' and '### Removed: Astro.locals.runtime API'

facts.claim: GitHub App private keys are PKCS#1 ('BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY'); WebCrypto importKey only accepts 'pkcs8'. The official universal-github-app-jwt THROWS on PKCS#1 in WebCrypto runtimes rather than converting.
facts.evidence: docs.github.com managing-private-keys-for-github-apps.md L36: 'the PEM file you download will be in `PKCS#1 RSAPrivateKey` format.'; gr2m/universal-github-app-jwt lib/get-token.js throws '[universal-github-app-jwt] Private Key is in PKCS#1 format, but only PKCS#8 is supported'; lib/crypto-native.js convertPrivateKey is a documented no-op
facts.impact: Either convert once with openssl and store PKCS#8 in the secret, or wrap PKCS#1 in a PKCS#8 header in JS (snippet 'worker-github-app.ts' does this; I ran it under Node WebCrypto against both key formats and verified the RS256 signature).

facts.claim: JWT claims: alg RS256, iss = app ID or client ID, iat set 60s in the past for clock drift, exp no more than 10 minutes out. Exchange at POST /app/installations/{installation_id}/access_tokens with Authorization: Bearer <JWT>. Installation token lasts 1 hour.
facts.evidence: docs.github.com generating-a-json-web-token-jwt-for-a-github-app: 'The time must be no more than 10 minutes into the future.' / 'we recommend that you set this 60 seconds in the past'; data/reusables/apps/generate-installation-access-token.md; authenticating-as-a-github-app-installation.md 'The installation access token will expire after 1 hour.'
facts.impact: Cache the installation token in module scope per isolate; do not mint one per request.

facts.claim: Installation id is discoverable with GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/installation (also /orgs/{org}/installation, /users/{u}/installation, /app/installations).
facts.evidence: data/reusables/apps/generate-installation-access-token.md

If it doesn't start with refs and have at least two slashes, it will be rejected.'; docs.github.com/rest/git/trees parameter table

  /* CLS: reserve the canvas box BEFORE any JS runs. A canvas with no intrinsic size
     is the classic layout-shift source on a configurator page. */
  .stage { position: relative; width: 100%; aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; contain: layout paint; }
  .stage > canvas { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; display: block; }
</style>

<!-- TBT is 30% of the mobile score and canvas bootstrap is the usual culprit.
     Never run the renderer during initial paint. -->
<script type="module">
  const stage = document.querySelector(".stage");
  const start = () => import("/js/configurator.js").then((m) => m.mount(stage));
  if ("IntersectionObserver" in window) {
    new IntersectionObserver((e, o) => { if (e[0].isIntersecting) { o.disconnect();
      (window.requestIdleCallback ?? setTimeout)(start, { timeout: 2000 }); } },
      { rootMargin: "200px" }).observe(stage);

</script>

gotchas: Navigation vs fetch on Workers assets: with compatibility_date >= 2025-04-01, typing /api/foo in the address bar serves HTML instead of hitting your Worker. Only run_worker_first (or the assets_navigation_has_no_effect flag) makes API paths behave.

`assets.directory` alone (no `main`) is billed as zero requests; adding `main` means every non-asset request is a billable Worker invocation. run_worker_first:true would make EVERY request billable — use the array form.
Astro 6+/adapter v13+ moved the wrangler `main` to '@astrojs/cloudflare/entrypoints/server' and deleted Astro.locals.runtime. Every blog post older than 2026 gets both wrong.

astro dev now runs in workerd, so CommonJS-only dependencies break in dev that previously worked; workaround is optimizeDeps.include in a Vite plugin, or prerenderEnvironment: 'node' for prerender-time Node APIs.
GitHub hands you a PKCS#1 key; WebCrypto only imports PKCS#8. universal-github-app-jwt does NOT convert it in Workers — it throws. Either openssl-convert once or use the DER wrapper in the snippet.
GH_PRIVATE_KEY stored via `wrangler secret put` or a .dev.vars often arrives with literal \\n; normalize before parsing the PEM.
Stripe: capture_method lives under payment_intent_data, which is payment-mode only. There is no top-level capture_method on a Checkout Session.
A manual-capture hold is not a 30-day escrow: Visa MIT is 4d18h, everything else ~7 days. After that the PaymentIntent goes to `canceled` on its own.
Stripe's new Trial Offer API explicitly does not support Checkout; use legacy subscription_data.trial_period_days + trial_end=now.
Turnstile tokens are single-use and expire in 300s; a user who leaves the form open then submits gets timeout-or-duplicate. Call turnstile.reset() on a stale form.
Turnstile secret must never reach the client; siteverify has to be called from the Worker only.
A <canvas> can never be the LCP element. Optimizing the canvas will not move LCP — the hero text and its font will.
Instrument Serif has no bold on Google Fonts. font-weight:700 silently renders faux bold, which also shifts metrics.
font-display:swap plus a metric mismatch is a CLS source; set size-adjust/ascent-override against your fallback stack or the 25%-weighted CLS audit bites.
Cloudflare can buffer compressed text/event-stream; force identity encoding and send a ':keepalive' comment every ~15s.
Workers runtime updates land a few times a week and kill in-flight requests after a 30s grace period, so a long SSE stream WILL drop. Emit id: lines and handle Last-Event-ID.
Polling GitHub from inside an SSE handler burns installation rate limit per connected viewer. Fan out through a Durable Object so one poller serves all viewers of a build.
blockers: PREMISE CONTRADICTED — 'Cloudflare Pages or Workers Static Assets': it is Workers. @astrojs/cloudflare v13+ removed Pages support outright, so 'Astro on Pages' is not a choice you have with the current adapter.

PREMISE CONTRADICTED — 'static output + separate Worker, or adapter with SSR routes': the actual current answer is neither as phrased. It is ONE Worker with assets.directory = ./dist plus main = ./worker/index.ts, no adapter, with run_worker_first for /api/*. Two separate Workers is the legacy Pages-era shape.

PREMISE CONTRADICTED — 'LCP with a canvas': a <canvas> is not an LCP candidate element in the spec. On a canvas-heavy page the score is dominated by TBT (30% weight, canvas bootstrap JS under 4x CPU throttling), with LCP driven by hero text/font. Budget accordingly.

HARD BLOCKER — real-time GitHub Actions job output. GET /actions/jobs/{job_id}/logs 404s while the job is running and only returns a 302 (60s-lived URL) after completion; there is no streaming log endpoint and no GitHub staff answer on community discussion #154834. You cannot build a live console off the logs API. Two workable substitutes: (1) poll GET /actions/runs/{run_id}/jobs every 2-3s and emit step-level transitions as SSE — reliable but coarse (per-step, not per-line); (2) have the workflow itself push lines to your Worker (a `run:` step piping through `tee` + curl to an authenticated /api/ingest endpoint backed by a Durable Object), which is the only way to get line-level output live. Plan on (2) if the console must show actual log text.

PARTIAL BLOCKER — compressed SSE buffering on Cloudflare is an open, unmerged workerd PR (#7390, opened 2026-09-16). Until it lands you must send SSE identity-encoded; do not assume brotli/gzip SSE flushes per event.

NOT ACHIEVABLE AS ASKED — manual capture on the per-device subscription. capture_method:manual is payment-mode only, so you cannot authorize-then-capture a subscription's first invoice. Use trial_period_days + trial_end=now after the passing build, or a separate $79 payment-mode session for the one-time item.

area: Fedora/KDE Plasma 6 bootc image: making Plasma feel like Windows to a non-technical user (system-wide defaults, kiosk lockdown, zero-terminal software install, first-boot onboarding)

facts.claim: `plasma-apply-layoutscript` does not exist in Plasma 6 (nor in Plasma 5.27). plasma-workspace ships only plasma-apply-colorscheme, plasma-apply-cursortheme, plasma-apply-desktoptheme, plasma-apply-lookandfeel, plasma-apply-wallpaperimage, plus lookandfeeltool and plasma-interactiveconsole.
facts.evidence: Arch plasma-workspace 6.7.5 file list (https://archlinux.org/packages/extra/x86_64/plasma-workspace/files/) shows usr/bin/plasma-apply-{colorscheme,cursortheme,desktoptheme,lookandfeel,wallpaperimage} and no plasma-apply-layoutscript; recursive git-tree greps of KDE/plasma-workspace master and Plasma/5.27 for 'layoutscript' return zero paths.
facts.impact: Remove `plasma-apply-layoutscript` from the design. Layout must be shipped through (a) a Look-and-Feel package layout script, (b) a custom shell package's layout.js, or (c) /etc/skel. For live re-application on a running session, the only scripted route is the D-Bus method org.kde.PlasmaShell.evaluateScript.

facts.claim: plasmashell chooses the first-run layout script in this exact order: `<LnF pkg>/contents/layouts/org.kde.plasma.desktop-prelayout.js` (pre-startup), then `<LnF pkg>/contents/layouts/org.kde.plasma.desktop-layout.js`, then the shell package's `defaultlayout` file. It only runs when the user has no existing containments.
facts.evidence: ShellCorona::loadDefaultLayout() in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KDE/plasma-workspace/master/shell/shellcorona.cpp lines ~1073-1115: `script = m_lookAndFeelPackage.filePath("layouts", QString(shell() + u"-prelayout.js"))` ... `script = m_lookAndFeelPackage.filePath("layouts", QString(shell() + u"-layout.js")); if (script.isEmpty()) script = kPackage().filePath("defaultlayout");`
facts.impact: The supported, image-native way to ship a Windows-like taskbar to every new user is a custom Look-and-Feel (Global Theme) package installed to /usr/share/plasma/look-and-feel/<id>/ containing contents/layouts/org.kde.plasma.desktop-layout.js, selected by default via /etc/xdg/kdeglobals [KDE] LookAndFeelPackage.

facts.claim: `defaultlayout` in the Plasma/Shell KPackage structure maps to the literal filename `layout.js` inside the shell package, and shell packages live under `plasma/shells/`. The stock desktop shell package is installed at /usr/share/plasma/shells/org.kde.plasma.desktop/.
facts.evidence: libplasma src/plasma/packagestructure/shell/shellpackage.cpp: `package->setDefaultPackageRoot(QStringLiteral("plasma/shells/"));` and `package->addFileDefinition("defaultlayout", QStringLiteral("layout.js"));` `package->addFileDefinition("defaults", QStringLiteral("defaults"));`. Arch plasma-desktop file list shows usr/share/plasma/shells/org.kde.plasma.desktop/contents/.
facts.impact: A second, heavier option: ship our own shell package /usr/share/plasma/shells/com.example.shell/contents/layout.js and select it with plasmashellrc [Shell] ShellPackage= or the env var PLASMA_DEFAULT_SHELL (set from /etc/xdg/plasma-workspace/env/*.sh). Note the current plasma-desktop desktoppackage ships main.js, not layout.js, so the stock shell package contributes no default layout - the Breeze LnF does.

facts.claim: The shell package name is resolved from plasmashellrc [Shell] ShellPackage, defaulting to the env var PLASMA_DEFAULT_SHELL, defaulting to org.kde.plasma.desktop.
facts.evidence: ShellCorona::defaultShell(): `const QString defaultValue = qEnvironmentVariable("PLASMA_DEFAULT_SHELL", u"org.kde.plasma.desktop"_s); QString value = startupConfGroup.readEntry("ShellPackage", defaultValue);`
facts.impact: Gives us a legitimate use for /etc/xdg/plasma-workspace/env/ if we go the custom-shell-package route.

facts.claim: `/etc/xdg/plasma-workspace/env/*.sh` is real and is sourced at Plasma session start, from every XDG config location, lowest-priority directory first, lexically by filename within a directory. It is for environment variables only.
facts.evidence: startkde/startplasma.cpp runEnvironmentScripts(): iterates QStandardPaths::GenericConfigLocation in reverse, `dir.cd(QStringLiteral("./plasma-workspace/env"))`, `dir.entryInfoList({QStringLiteral("*.sh")}, QDir::Files, QDir::Name)`. Comment: "Source scripts found in <config locations>/plasma-workspace/env/*.sh".
facts.impact: Use it for PLASMA_DEFAULT_SHELL / QT_* / toolkit env only. It cannot create config files or panels - do not try to seed the layout from here.

facts.claim: `/etc/xdg/plasma-org.kde.plasma.desktop-appletsrc` does NOT work. Plasma opens the applets/containment config with KConfig::SimpleConfig, which disables the XDG cascade entirely.
facts.evidence: libplasma src/plasma/corona.cpp: `d->config = KSharedConfig::openConfig(d->configName, KConfig::SimpleConfig);` (Corona::config()) and `c = KSharedConfig::openConfig(configName, KConfig::SimpleConfig);` in Corona::saveLayout().
facts.impact: Blocker for the obvious approach. Panel/widget layout can only be seeded per-user: /etc/skel/.config/plasma-org.kde.plasma.desktop-appletsrc, or generated at first login by the LnF layout script. Everything else in kdeglobals/kwinrc/dolphinrc DOES cascade from /etc/xdg.

facts.claim: KConfig parses files "from the least to the most specific", and startplasma inserts ~/.config/kdedefaults at the FRONT of XDG_CONFIG_DIRS, ahead of /etc/xdg. The Look-and-Feel package's `contents/defaults` are written into ~/.config/kdedefaults at every session start when the active LnF changes.
facts.evidence: kconfig/src/core/kconfig.cpp: `// Parse all desired files from the least to the most specific.` then parseGlobalSystemFiles -> parseSystemConfigFiles -> parseGlobalUserFiles -> parseUserConfigFiles. startplasma.cpp setupPlasmaEnvironment(): `const QString extraConfigDir = ... + QLatin1String("/kdedefaults"); qputenv("XDG_CONFIG_DIRS", QByteArray(QFile::encodeName(extraConfigDir) + ':' + currentConfigDirs));` then `lnfManager.setMode(KLookAndFeelManager::Mode::Defaults); lnfManager.save(package, lookAndFeelContents);`
facts.impact: Any appearance key we set in /etc/xdg/kdeglobals will be silently overridden by the active Global Theme's `defaults` unless we either (a) put it in our own LnF package's contents/defaults, or (b) mark it immutable with [$i] in /etc/xdg/kdeglobals. Prefer (a) for appearance, (b) for policy.

facts.claim: The default Global Theme is chosen by kdeglobals [KDE] LookAndFeelPackage (default org.kde.breeze.desktop). Related keys: DefaultLightLookAndFeel, DefaultDarkLookAndFeel, AutomaticLookAndFeel.
facts.evidence: plasma-workspace/kcms/lookandfeel/lookandfeelsettings.kcfg: `<kcfgfile name="kdeglobals" /> <group name="KDE"> <entry name="lookAndFeelPackage" key="LookAndFeelPackage" type="String"><default>org.kde.breeze.desktop</default>`
facts.impact: One line in /etc/xdg/kdeglobals sets our Windows-like theme for every user, including users created after the image is updated.

facts.claim: A Look-and-Feel package's `contents/defaults` is an INI whose group headers are `[<configfile>][<group>]`, and it is what actually sets widget style, color scheme, icon theme, Plasma style, cursors, window decoration, splash and wallpaper.
facts.evidence: plasma-workspace/lookandfeel/org.kde.breeze/contents/defaults, fetched verbatim (see snippet 'lookandfeel-defaults-breeze'). Same structure confirmed in the third-party Windows-11-style theme doncsugar/willow-theme global-themes/org.kde.willow-light.desktop/contents/defaults.
facts.impact: This is the single file that carries our whole 'looks like Windows' appearance bundle; it ships in /usr and is applied automatically at session start.

facts.claim: Plasma 6 ALREADY defaults to double-click. kdeglobals [KDE] SingleClick default is false.
facts.evidence: plasma-desktop/kcms/workspaceoptions/workspaceoptions_kdeglobalssettings.kcfg: `<kcfgfile name="kdeglobals" /><group name="KDE"><entry name="singleClick" key="SingleClick" type="Bool"><label>Single click to open files</label><default>false</default></entry>`
facts.impact: Requirement 3's premise is wrong for Plasma 6. Setting SingleClick=false is a no-op we can still write defensively. The Windows-parity keys actually worth setting in the same group are DndBehavior=MoveIfSameDevice (Windows moves within a drive instead of showing a drop menu) and DoubleClickInterval.

facts.claim: Kiosk action restrictions live in `[KDE Action Restrictions]` in kdeglobals (and per-app rc files), and per-group/per-key immutability is expressed with the `[$i]` suffix. The system-wide cascade is ~/.config/<app>rc, /etc/xdg/<app>rc, ~/.config/kdeglobals, /etc/xdg/kdeglobals, ~/.config/system.kdeglobals, /etc/xdg/system.kdeglobals, /etc/kde5rc.
facts.evidence: https://develop.kde.org/docs/administration/kiosk/introduction/ - gives the cascade list, `[KDE Action Restrictions][$i]` syntax, `widgetStyle[$i]=breeze`, `[KDE][$i]`, and `[KDE Control Module Restrictions][$i] kcm_mouse=false` in /etc/kde5rc.
facts.impact: Gives us the exact file and syntax for the 'locked' and 'kiosk' policy modes.

facts.claim: The kiosk key set that is demonstrably still honoured by Plasma 6 / KF6 code (not just KDE4-era docs): `logout` + `action/logout`, `action/start_new_session`, `action/lock_screen`, `run_command`, `shell_access`, `action/kwin_rmb`, `plasma/plasmashell/unlockedDesktop`, `plasma-desktop/scripting_console`.
facts.evidence: plasma-workspace/libkworkspace/sessionmanagement.cpp: canLogout() `KAuthorized::authorizeAction("logout") && KAuthorized::authorize("logout")` with comment "checking both is for compatibility with old kiosk configs"; canSwitchUser() `authorizeAction("start_new_session")`; canLock() `authorizeAction("lock_screen")`. krunner/main.cpp: `if (!KAuthorized::authorize(u"run_command"_s))`. kwin/src/useractions.cpp: `if (!KAuthorized::authorizeAction(QStringLiteral("kwin_rmb")))`. dolphin/src/dolphinmainwindow.cpp lines 2204 and 2443: `KAuthorized::authorize(QStringLiteral("shell_access"))`. shellcorona.cpp:843 `KAuthorized::authorize("plasma/plasmashell/unlockedDesktop")`, :1990 `"plasma-desktop/scripting_console"`.
facts.impact: These are safe to ship. Note authorizeAction("X") reads the key `action/X`, so logout needs BOTH `logout=false` and `action/logout=false`.

facts.claim: The full documented restriction-key list also includes: custom_config, editable_desktop_icons, lineedit_text_completion, lineedit_reveal_password, movable_toolbars, run_desktop_files, skip_drm, action/switch_user, action/options_configure, action/options_configure_keybinding, action/options_configure_toolbars, action/options_configure_notifications, action/help_report_bug, action/help_about_kde, action/switch_application_language, action/bookmarks, action/openwith, action/editfiletype, action/properties, action/show_dot, action/executeshellcommand, action/kdesktop_rmb, action/konsole_rmb, ghns, plasma/allow_configure_when_locked, plasma/containment_actions, plasma-desktop/add_activities, opengl_screensavers, manipulatescreen_screensavers, plus print/{copies,dialog,options,properties,selection,system}, and the `[KDE Resource Restrictions]` group.
facts.evidence: https://develop.kde.org/docs/administration/kiosk/keys/ (official KDE developer docs) - full tables reproduced.
facts.impact: Gives the menu to pick from for 'locked' vs 'kiosk'. Caveat: many entries in that page are KDE4-era and target konqiconviewrc/konsolerc, apps we will not ship; treat anything not in the previous fact as unverified for Plasma 6.

facts.claim: KConfig's hardcoded system-wide rc file is still literally `/etc/kde5rc` in current KF6 master - there is no /etc/kde6rc.
facts.evidence: kconfig/src/core/kconfig.cpp: `etc_kderc = ... QStringLiteral("/etc/kde5rc");` guarded by KDE_SKIP_KDERC.
facts.impact: `[KDE Control Module Restrictions]` (hiding System Settings pages) must go in /etc/kde5rc, not /etc/kde6rc. This is a trap; the file name looks stale but is correct.

facts.claim: Discover has NO configuration key to enable or disable backends. Backends are QPluginLoader plugins discovered by scanning `<qt plugin dirs>/discover/*.so`; the only selection mechanism is the `--backends` command-line option.
facts.evidence: discover/libdiscover/DiscoverBackendsFactory.cpp: allBackendNames() does `QDirIterator it(dir + QStringLiteral("/discover"), QDir::Files)` over QCoreApplication::libraryPaths(); the only override is setRequestedBackends() fed from `parser->value(QStringLiteral("backends")).split(',')` via the `--backends` option. discover/discoversettings.kcfg only defines DiscoverUI sorting keys in discoverrc.
facts.impact: To hide the rpm/dnf path we must either not install the plugin RPM, delete the .so in the Containerfile, or override the .desktop Exec with --backends. Any 'discoverrc backend' key we might invent does not exist.

facts.claim: Fedora splits Discover backends into separate RPMs with exact plugin paths: plasma-discover-packagekit -> %{_kf6_qtplugindir}/discover/packagekit-backend.so; plasma-discover-flatpak -> flatpak-backend.so; plasma-discover-rpm-ostree -> rpm-ostree-backend.so; plasma-discover-snap -> snap-backend.so; plasma-discover-kns -> kns-backend.so; plasma-discover-libs carries appstream-preview-backend.so and (when built) fwupd-backend.so.
facts.evidence: src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/plasma-discover rawhide spec (version 6.7.90, changelog dated Thu Sep 10 2026), %files sections. %{_kf6_qtplugindir} resolves to /usr/lib64/qt6/plugins.
facts.impact: Cleanest zero-terminal store: install plasma-discover + plasma-discover-flatpak + plasma-discover-notifier + plasma-discover-offline-updates, and do NOT install plasma-discover-packagekit / -snap / -kns. Keep plasma-discover-rpm-ostree ONLY if you want Discover to offer OS updates - otherwise users get no GUI update path at all.

facts.claim: plasma-discover-rpm-ostree is Supplements-ed onto Kinoite-like systems: `Supplements: ((plasma-discover and rpm-ostree) unless dnf)`. It can therefore get pulled in implicitly.
facts.evidence: Same rawhide spec, %package rpm-ostree section.
facts.impact: On a Fedora bootc/Kinoite base it will already be installed. Removing it must be explicit (`dnf -y remove plasma-discover-rpm-ostree` or `rm` the .so) in the Containerfile.

facts.claim: Fedora ships /etc/xdg/discoverrc containing only `[Software] UseOfflineUpdates=true` (from the plasma-discover-offline-updates subpackage).
facts.evidence: src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/plasma-discover rawhide `discoverrc` source file, fetched verbatim; spec line `install -m644 -p -D %{SOURCE10} %{buildroot}%{_kf6_sysconfdir}/xdg/discoverrc` and `%files offline-updates %{_kf6_sysconfdir}/xdg/discoverrc`.
facts.impact: Confirms /etc/xdg/discoverrc is the right place for Discover system defaults, and that Windows-style 'install updates on restart' is already the Fedora default.

facts.claim: Flatpak auto-applies `.flatpakrepo` files dropped into `/etc/flatpak/remotes.d/` and `/usr/share/flatpak/remotes.d/` to the DEFAULT SYSTEM installation only (not user installs, not extra installations).
facts.evidence: flatpak/common/flatpak-dir.c `_flatpak_dir_find_new_flatpakrepos()`: `#define FLATPAK_REMOTES_DIR "remotes.d"`; early-return `if (self->user || (self->extra_data && g_strcmp0 (self->extra_data->id, SYSTEM_DIR_DEFAULT_ID) != 0)) return NULL;` with comment `/* Predefined remotes only applies for the default system installation */`; then scans get_config_dir_location()/remotes.d and get_data_dir_location()/remotes.d. meson.build sets FLATPAK_CONFIGDIR = prefix/sysconfdir/flatpak and FLATPAK_DATADIR = prefix/datadir/flatpak. Fedora's flatpak.spec creates and owns both %{_sysconfdir}/flatpak/remotes.d and %{_datadir}/flatpak/remotes.d.
facts.impact: This is the correct image-native way to preconfigure Flathub - a plain file in /usr, which survives bootc updates. No first-boot script needed just for the remote.

facts.claim: `flatpak preinstall` is the supported declarative way to ship a default app set: drop `.preinstall` files in /usr/share/flatpak/preinstall.d/ or /etc/flatpak/preinstall.d/; the OS runs `flatpak preinstall -y` at startup; users who uninstall an app do not get it reinstalled.
facts.evidence: flatpak doc/flatpak-preinstall.xml (man flatpak-preinstall): "Preinstalled flatpaks are defined by dropping .preinstall files into the directories /usr/share/flatpak/preinstall.d/ and /etc/flatpak/preinstall.d/. The OS runs flatpak preinstall -y (or its GUI equivalent) on system startup". Group format `[Flatpak Preinstall NAME]` with keys Install, Branch, IsRuntime, CollectionID. Fedora's flatpak.spec creates %{_datadir}/flatpak/preinstall.d and %{_sysconfdir}/flatpak/preinstall.d.
facts.impact: Ship Firefox/LibreOffice/VLC etc. as .preinstall files in /usr instead of a bespoke first-boot script. Combined with remotes.d this gives a fully declarative, zero-terminal app baseline.

facts.claim: In bootc, /var content from the image is unpacked ONLY from the initial image (Docker VOLUME semantics), while /etc gets a 3-way merge on every update.
facts.evidence: https://bootc.dev/bootc/filesystem.html: "content included in /var in the container image acts like a Docker VOLUME /var. This means its contents are unpacked only from the initial image - subsequent changes to /var in a container image are not automatically applied." and for /etc: "The new default /etc is used as a base", "The diff between current and previous /etc is applied to the new /etc", "Locally modified files in /etc different from the default /usr/etc (of the same deployment) will be retained."
facts.impact: System flatpaks live in /var/lib/flatpak and therefore CANNOT be baked into the image and cannot be updated by an image update. Preinstall/remotes.d in /usr is the only maintainable route. Also: /etc/xdg/* config we ship WILL be updated on image upgrade as long as the user hasn't edited it - good. /etc/skel content will update in /etc/skel but will NOT retroactively change existing users' home dirs.

facts.claim: plasma-welcome is the KDE-native first-run app and is already packaged in Fedora (rawhide 6.7.90), including its kded auto-launch module kded_plasma_welcome.so.
facts.evidence: src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/plasma-welcome rawhide spec: Name: plasma-welcome, Version: 6.7.90, %files includes %{_kf6_bindir}/plasma-welcome, %{_kf6_plugindir}/kded/kded_plasma_welcome.so, %{_kf6_datadir}/config.kcfg/plasma-welcome.kcfg. Changelog Thu Sep 10 2026.
facts.impact: Answers requirement 6: do not build a custom welcome app and do not reach for yafti (GTK, ublue-specific) or gnome-initial-setup (GNOME). Install plasma-welcome and extend it.

facts.claim: plasma-welcome is launched exactly once per user by a kded module, gated on `plasma-welcomerc [General] LastSeenVersion` being empty; the module writes the current version afterwards. It also relaunches with --post-update after a significant Plasma upgrade unless ShowUpdatePage=false.
facts.evidence: plasma-welcome src/kded/daemon.cpp: `const bool lastSeenVersionEmpty = m_configGroup.readEntry("LastSeenVersion", QStringLiteral("")).isEmpty(); if (lastSeenVersionEmpty) { launch(QStringList{}); } else if (m_configGroup.readEntry("ShowUpdatePage", true) && isSignificantUpgrade()) { launch(QStringList{QStringLiteral("--post-update")}); }` and `m_configGroup.writeEntry("LastSeenVersion", m_currentVersion.toString());`. Config schema src/config.kcfg: kcfgfile plasma-welcomerc, group General, entries LastSeenVersion, LiveEnvironment, LiveInstaller, ShowUpdatePage, AutomaticUpdatePreview.
facts.impact: Once-per-user triggering is free - install the package and do nothing. To suppress the post-update nag in a consumer product, ship /etc/xdg/plasma-welcomerc with ShowUpdatePage=false (KConfig cascade applies, since the daemon opens KConfig("plasma-welcomerc") with default cascading flags).

facts.claim: plasma-welcome is officially extensible without writing C++: custom intro text/icon at /usr/share/plasma/plasma-welcome/intro-customization.desktop, and extra wizard pages as numbered QML files in /usr/share/plasma/plasma-welcome/extra-pages/ (e.g. 01-WelcomeToDistro.qml). Pages may run shell commands via Controller.runCommand() and embed KCMs via KCMPage{ path: "kcm_..." }.
facts.evidence: plasma-welcome README.md (upstream), sections "Customizing the first page", "Extending Welcome Center with custom pages", "Run a terminal command", "Embed a KCM in the page".
facts.impact: We get a branded, Windows-OOBE-like first-run flow - name/printer/browser choice, app picker that shells out to flatpak install - with zero custom application code.

facts.claim: Folder names are controlled system-wide by /etc/xdg/user-dirs.defaults (DESKTOP, DOCUMENTS, DOWNLOAD, MUSIC, PICTURES, PROJECTS, PUBLICSHARE, TEMPLATES, VIDEOS) and behaviour by /etc/xdg/user-dirs.conf (enabled, filename_encoding). Values are relative to $HOME and are translated per-path-element into the user's locale.
facts.evidence: xdg-user-dirs man/user-dirs.defaults.xml: "The /etc/xdg/user-dirs.defaults file is a text file that contains the default values for the XDG user dirs which are used by the xdg-user-dirs-update command"; upstream data/user-dirs.defaults and data/user-dirs.conf fetched verbatim.
facts.impact: Documents/Desktop/Downloads are already the defaults and already Windows-like. We only need to drop Projects/Public/Templates if we want a tighter Windows-like set. Note PROJECTS is a newer upstream addition not present on older systems.

facts.claim: Dolphin's global view properties (view mode, sort, show-hidden) are stored per-user at ~/.local/share/dolphin/view_properties/global/.directory, not in a cascading config file. dolphinrc does cascade and holds the Explorer-relevant keys (ShowFullPath, EditableUrl, ShowStatusBar, RenameInline, AutoExpandFolders, GlobalViewProps, plus [DetailsMode] and [IconsMode] groups).
facts.evidence: dolphin src/views/viewproperties.cpp: `const char ViewPropertiesFileName[] = ".directory";`, `destinationDir()` = `QStandardPaths::writableLocation(QStandardPaths::AppDataLocation) + "/view_properties/" + subDir`, and `m_filePath = destinationDir(QStringLiteral("global"))`. dolphin src/settings/dolphin_generalsettings.kcfg and dolphin_detailsmodesettings.kcfg (kcfgfile name="dolphinrc").
facts.impact: Ship /etc/xdg/dolphinrc for the cascading half, and /etc/skel/.local/share/dolphin/view_properties/global/.directory to force a Windows-Explorer-like Details view by default. Existing users won't pick the latter up on image update.

facts.claim: Panel scripting API value strings for the layout script: alignment in {left, center, right}; lengthMode in {fill, fit, custom}; hiding in {normal(default), autohide, dodgewindows, windowsgobelow}; opacity in {adaptive, opaque, translucent}; plus floating, floatingApplets, height, offset, length, minimumLength, maximumLength, location, screen, locked.
facts.evidence: plasma-workspace/shell/scripting/panel.h Q_PROPERTY list and panel.cpp setAlignment/setLengthMode/setHiding/setOpacity/setFloating implementations, read verbatim.
facts.impact: Exact vocabulary for our Windows-11 layout.js. For a Win11 look: floating=false, opacity="opaque" or "translucent", hiding="normal".

facts.claim: Layout templates are KPackages rooted at plasma/layout-templates/ with mainscript = contents/layout.js and a metadata.json declaring "KPackageStructure": "Plasma/LayoutTemplate"; they are invoked from a layout script with loadTemplate("<Id>"). Stock ones are org.kde.plasma.desktop.defaultPanel, .emptyPanel, .appmenubar.
facts.evidence: plasma-workspace/shell/packageplugins/layouttemplate/layouttemplate.cpp: `setDefaultPackageRoot(QStringLiteral("plasma/layout-templates/")); addFileDefinition("mainscript", QStringLiteral("layout.js")); setRequired("mainscript", true);`. Arch plasma-desktop file list shows usr/share/plasma/layout-templates/org.kde.plasma.desktop.defaultPanel/{metadata.json,contents/layout.js}. Breeze LnF layout script is literally `loadTemplate("org.kde.plasma.desktop.defaultPanel")`.
facts.impact: Lets us ship the Windows-11 taskbar as a reusable template that also shows up in the user's right-click 'Add Panel' menu, and keep the LnF layout script to two lines.

facts.claim: Relevant applet IDs and their default config keys for a Windows-like taskbar: org.kde.plasma.kickoff (icon, menuLabel, favorites, systemFavorites, primaryActions, favoritesDisplay 0=Grid/1=List, applicationsDisplay, compactMode, paneSwap); org.kde.plasma.icontasks (X-Plasma-RootPath org.kde.plasma.taskmanager, keys launchers, groupingStrategy, showOnlyCurrentDesktop, onlyGroupWhenFull, middleClickAction, minimizeActiveTaskOnClick); org.kde.plasma.panelspacer (expanding bool default true, length int); org.kde.plasma.systemtray; org.kde.plasma.digitalclock; org.kde.plasma.showdesktop; org.kde.plasma.marginsseparator.
facts.evidence: plasma-desktop/applets/kickoff/main.xml, applets/taskmanager/main.xml, applets/icontasks/metadata.json, plasma-workspace/applets/panelspacer/main.xml - all read verbatim from invent.kde.org raw.
facts.impact: Gives us the exact writeConfig() keys for layout.js, including the Windows-11 centering trick (a panelspacer with expanding=true on each side of the launcher+tasks block).

facts.claim: Fedora's own pattern for adding flatpak remotes on a bootc/atomic system is a oneshot systemd unit guarded by a stamp file under /var/lib/flatpak.
facts.evidence: src.fedoraproject.org/rpms/flatpak rawhide Source1 flatpak-add-fedora-repos.service, fetched verbatim (see snippet). Uses ConditionPathExists=!/var/lib/flatpak/.fedora-initialized, Before=flatpak-system-helper.service, ExecStartPost=touch stamp.

facts.claim: Realistic Windows-11-style Plasma theming exists only as third-party Global Themes; the KDE Store item 'Windows Eleven Plasma 6' and the GitHub project doncsugar/willow-theme are the main candidates. Willow is GPL-3.0 and ships aurorae window decorations, color schemes, a Plasma style, SDDM theme, icons and a proper global-theme package, but its README requires manual steps (install the Lightly application style, change Dolphin's toolbar, adjust Aurorae) and it is not labelled Plasma 6.

// Windows 11 style: full-width opaque bottom bar, Start + pinned apps centered,
// system tray + clock + show-desktop on the right.
// Centering is done with two expanding org.kde.plasma.panelspacer widgets,
// which works regardless of how panel.alignment interacts with lengthMode.

var panel = new Panel
panel.location = "bottom"

// Round up to an even number of pixels; the panel size UI only shows even values.
panel.height = 2 * Math.ceil(gridUnit * 2.5 / 2)

panel.lengthMode = "fill"        // fill | fit | custom
panel.alignment  = "center"      // left | center | right
panel.hiding     = "normal"      // normal | autohide | dodgewindows | windowsgobelow
panel.floating   = false         // Windows 11's taskbar is edge-anchored, not floating
panel.opacity    = "opaque"      // adaptive | opaque | translucent

// --- left spacer (pushes the Start+tasks block to the middle) ---
var leftSpacer = panel.addWidget("org.kde.plasma.panelspacer")
leftSpacer.currentConfigGroup = ["General"]
leftSpacer.writeConfig("expanding", true)

// --- Start menu ---
var kickoff = panel.addWidget("org.kde.plasma.kickoff")
kickoff.currentConfigGroup = ["General"]
kickoff.writeConfig("icon", "start-here-kde-symbolic")
kickoff.writeConfig("menuLabel", "")
kickoff.writeConfig("favoritesDisplay", 0)        // 0 = Grid  (Win11 "Pinned")
kickoff.writeConfig("applicationsDisplay", 1)     // 1 = List  (Win11 "All apps")
kickoff.writeConfig("primaryActions", 0)          // 0 = Power buttons in footer
kickoff.writeConfig("showActionButtonCaptions", true)
kickoff.writeConfig("alphaSort", true)
kickoff.writeConfig("favorites",
    "preferred://browser,org.kde.dolphin.desktop,org.kde.discover.desktop,systemsettings.desktop")
kickoff.writeConfig("systemFavorites", "suspend,reboot,shutdown")

// --- Taskbar (icons only, like Windows 11) ---
var tasks = panel.addWidget("org.kde.plasma.icontasks")
tasks.currentConfigGroup = ["General"]
tasks.writeConfig("launchers",
    "applications:org.kde.dolphin.desktop,preferred://browser,applications:org.kde.discover.desktop")
tasks.writeConfig("groupingStrategy", 1)          // group by program
tasks.writeConfig("onlyGroupWhenFull", false)     // Win11 always groups
tasks.writeConfig("showOnlyCurrentDesktop", false)
tasks.writeConfig("showOnlyCurrentActivity", false)
tasks.writeConfig("minimizeActiveTaskOnClick", true)
tasks.writeConfig("middleClickAction", 2)         // new instance
tasks.writeConfig("fill", false)

// --- right spacer ---
var rightSpacer = panel.addWidget("org.kde.plasma.panelspacer")
rightSpacer.currentConfigGroup = ["General"]
rightSpacer.writeConfig("expanding", true)

// --- right-hand "notification area" ---
panel.addWidget("org.kde.plasma.systemtray")

var clock = panel.addWidget("org.kde.plasma.digitalclock")
clock.currentConfigGroup = ["Appearance"]
clock.writeConfig("showDate", true)
clock.writeConfig("dateFormat", "shortDate")

// Windows' far-right "Show desktop" sliver
panel.addWidget("org.kde.plasma.showdesktop")

FROM quay.io/fedora/fedora-kinoite:43

# 1. Keep only the Flatpak backend. plasma-discover-rpm-ostree is pulled in by a
#    weak dep on Kinoite (Supplements: ((plasma-discover and rpm-ostree) unless dnf))
#    so it must be removed explicitly.
RUN dnf -y install plasma-discover plasma-discover-flatpak \
                   plasma-discover-notifier plasma-discover-offline-updates \
                   plasma-welcome flatpak && \
    dnf -y remove  plasma-discover-packagekit plasma-discover-snap \
                   plasma-discover-kns plasma-discover-rpm-ostree || true

# 2. Belt and braces: the factory only enumerates *.so under <plugindir>/discover,
#    there is no config key to disable a backend.
RUN rm -f /usr/lib64/qt6/plugins/discover/packagekit-backend.so \
          /usr/lib64/qt6/plugins/discover/rpm-ostree-backend.so \
          /usr/lib64/qt6/plugins/discover/snap-backend.so \
          /usr/lib64/qt6/plugins/discover/kns-backend.so \
          /usr/lib64/qt6/plugins/discover-notifier/DiscoverPackageKitNotifier.so \
          /usr/lib64/qt6/plugins/discover-notifier/rpm-ostree-notifier.so

# 3. Flathub, declaratively, in /usr so it survives image updates.
RUN mkdir -p /usr/share/flatpak/remotes.d && \
    curl -fsSL -o /usr/share/flatpak/remotes.d/flathub.flatpakrepo \
      https://dl.flathub.org/repo/flathub.flatpakrepo

COPY usr/ /usr/
RUN bootc container lint
